Hague court orders India to uphold Indus Waters Treaty, suspend work on its hydropower project. The Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) on Monday ordered India to uphold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir. Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025. Following India’s move, Pakistan termed any attempt to suspend its water share an “act of war”, noting the IWT had no provision for unilateral suspension. It later argued that Delhi’s action was a violation of the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties. In its order, the PCA backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement. The Hague-based court issued an award on the status of the IWT “in respect of India’s decision on abeyance” and an order on Pakistan’s application dated March 4 regarding “interim measures” concerning the Ratle hydro-electric plant. In a press release detailing its ruling, the PCA said it “examined the potential grounds upon which India could suspend or terminate the treaty, including the grounds cited by India in its public statements”. “In a unanimous decision, the court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the treaty.” It declared that the IWT “remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers”. The IWT allocates the eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — to India, while the western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — are largely allocated to Pakistan. The 1960 water-sharing agreement has also established mechanisms for data-sharing and dispute resolution. During the proceedings, Pakistan requested the court to address the “design of certain components of the run-of-river hydro-electric projects that India is permitted by the IWT to construct on the Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab rivers and their tributaries (“western rivers”), before those rivers flow into Pakistan”, the PCA statement said. The proceedings in the interim measures’ application concerned India’s Kishenganga Hydro-Electric Plant (KHEP) and the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant (RHEP). The court noted that the Kishenganga and Ratle plants were “also the subject of proceedings” before a World Bank-appointed neutral expert, who is expected to issue a final decision in July 2027 on whether they were in line with the IWT. In its order, the PCA unanimously decided to “impose measures prohibiting India from concreting the RHEP dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels until 90 days after the neutral expert’s final decision”. The court also imposed a reporting measure related to the RHEP Construction Schedule until shortly after the neutral expert’s final decision. It declined to grant two other measures requested by Pakistan. The PCA noted that the IWT “does not provide for one party to terminate or suspend the operation of the treaty, or for ‘abeyance’”. The IWT provides that it will remain in force unless modified or terminated by India and Pakistan acting together through adoption of a further treaty. The Court of Arbitration was chaired by Professor Sean D. Murphy of the United States. The other members were Professor Wouter Buytaert of Belgium, Professor Jeffrey P. Minear of the United States, Judge Awn Shawkat Al-Khasawneh of Jordan, and Dr Donald Blackmore of Australia. Pakistan welcomes findings Islamabad “took note” of the press release and welcomed the PCA’s finding that India “remains bound by and must observe its obligations under” the IWT, the information ministry said. It also welcomed the finding regarding the Ratle plant, as well as the measures ordered by the court. The government “will now be giving careful consideration to the detail of the award and decision, pending their publication, and how these may best assist in finding a pathway back to the parties’ engagement under the treaty”, the statement added. India, which is officially a member of the intergovernmental court, said it did not recognise the court and “categorically” rejected the verdict. “This so-called Court of Arbitration has no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions,” India’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement. While India did not participate by making written or oral submissions in response to Pakistan’s application, the PCA sought to consider India’s positions on the matters “to the extent they could be discerned from India’s statements and conduct outside of these proceedings (including Indian government communications to Pakistan and to the neutral expert, and public statements made by Indian officials)”. India has no grounds to suspend IWT The PCA examined possible grounds for India’s action outside the treaty — ie under customary international law rules — but found that “there is no rule allowing a state to unilaterally terminate or suspend the operation of a treaty based on its ‘sovereignty’”, as argued by India. The court considered several potential arguments based on India’s statements, but found that they did not justify New Delhi’s actions to suspend the IWT. It identified three of the “few, highly restricted grounds” upon which a state could unilaterally terminate or suspend the operation of a treaty: material breach of the pact by a party, fundamental change of circumstances, and effect of armed conflict. On India’s claim that Pakistan had violated the IWT’s “cooperative spirit” by failing to enter into negotiations to modify the treaty, the court found that “no provision of the treaty obliged Pakistan to enter into such” discussions and therefore, this cannot be a material breach of the IWT. In fact, after examining the correspondence between the two governments, the court said it “found that Pakistan had been willing to discuss with India the issue of treaty modifications”. On India’s allegations of cross-border terrorism, which New Delhi had cited while unilaterally suspending the IWT last year, the PCA observed that the treaty “does not address terrorism or the use of force and expressly indicates that it governs only” the rights and obligations regarding the Indus waters. The court said it “did not find evidence that the alleged terrorism had impeded India’s ability to construct its HEPs on the western rivers and instead noted that India has built and is building many such HEPs, including in recent years”. “Even if India’s allegation was assumed to be true, they would not establish a material breach of the treaty by Pakistan,” it said. Regarding possible fundamental change of circumstances, the court considered India’s arguments of “(1) demographic changes; (2) the need for clean energy in India; (3) changes in dam infrastructure technology; (4) escalating cross-border terrorist attacks; and (5) the effects of climate change”. However, in each instance, the court found that the “necessary conditions for invoking a ‘fundamental change of circumstances’ under the law of treaties had not been met”. The court pointed out that the IWT “was of a type that would remain operational” even during an armed conflict, adding that such a conflict did not exist at present. Furthermore, the PCA also considered whether India’s conduct could be justified “as a ‘countermeasure’ against an antecedent violation of international law by Pakistan”, but found that the requirements for a lawful countermeasure had not been met. The court ruled that a “termination or suspension of the operation of the treaty would affect India’s obligations to protect fundamental human rights, would not permit the resumption of India’s obligations under the treaty, and would preclude the operation of dispute settlement provisions under the treaty”. Timeline of proceedings Pakistan had initiated the arbitration proceedings regarding the western rivers in August 2016, the PCA press release recalled. However, in December that year, the World Bank decided to “ pause ” the process of appointing the chairman of the Court of Arbitration and the neutral expert. This pause was lifted in 2022, following which a neutral expert was appointed. After India unilaterally held the IWT in abeyance in April 2025, the PCA considered its effect on the court’s competence in a “Supplemental Award on Competence” issued on June 27 that year. The court held that “India’s decision on the ‘abeyance’ of the treaty cannot limit the competence of the Court over this dispute”. “However, the court did not go further in determining whether the Indus Waters Treaty remained in force,” it added. On March 4, Pakistan filed an application before the court to “determine the present status of the Treaty in light of India’s decision on ‘abeyance’”. The PCA noted that India was invited to indicate whether it would participate in the proceedings but received “no response”. The court then directed Pakistan to “file a written memorial further detailing its application and held a hearing at the Peace Palace in The Hague” from April 26 to 28. Additional input from Reuters

Lionel Messi says retiring from international football. Lionel Messi said on Monday he is retiring from international football after leading Argentina to a second successive World Cup final in July. Following the death of his father Jorge in August, Messi had said he had “serious doubts” about continuing to play football of any sort for “much longer”. “It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep in my soul, but I understand that it is the right time,” Messi, 39, wrote on Instagram. In the post, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner notes that he wrote these words two days after Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on July 19. “After what happened with my father, I am more convinced than ever,” he added. View this post on Instagram Messi swore that he “always gave everything” to his fans and “not just during these last few years when we won everything, but before that as well”. “I always fought and gave my all for this shirt, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football,” he wrote. “There isn’t much time left, and chapters are gradually coming to a close, and this is one that hurts me a lot,” Messi added, expressing his love for the Argentine national team. “I gave everything I had; I have nothing more left to give. And besides, there are some very talented young players coming through who deserve to be there.” The football icon expressed gratitude to his fans for their support over the past two decades, as well as his family, coaches and teammates. “Now I’ll be one of you, always cheering and supporting from the outside (in good times and bad, even more so),” he added, addressing his fans. “I leave with the peace of mind and pride of having given you, together with my teammates, moments we could only have dreamed of. It was crazy to have lived it all with you. I love you!” Messi led Argentina to World Cup glory by winning the 2022 final against France in a penalty shootout in Qatar. His contract with Major League Soccer club Inter Miami runs until the end of the 2028 season.

PM Shehbaz meets Iranian President Pezeshkian on sidelines of SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State meeting on Monday, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). PM Shehbaz arrived in Bishkek earlier today on a three-day official visit from Aug 31 to Sep 2, at the invitation of President Sadyr Nurgozhoevich Zhaparov to attend the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting. The leaders of China, Iran, Turkiye, Russia, and India were in Kyrgyzstan for the two-day SCO summit. The regional bloc, which also includes Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus, is celebrating its 25th anniversary. On the sidelines of the summit, PM Shehbaz and Pezeshkian held a “warm and cordial” meeting, during which they reaffirmed the close and longstanding ties between both countries, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. They emphasised the need to further strengthen bilateral relations across all areas of mutual cooperation, in line with decisions taken during the visit of President Pezeshkian to Pakistan in June this year. The leaders reviewed ongoing efforts aimed at enhancing regional connectivity and people-to-people contacts, as well as exchanged views on the evolving regional situation. While reaffirming that Pakistan would continue its sincere efforts for regional peacebuilding, PM Shehbaz said that the recent visit of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir to Tehran and his “constructive engagements augured well”, the PMO noted. The premier stressed the importance of restraint and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region. He also underscored the need to build on the understandings reached under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the United States and Iran on June 18. PM Shehbaz noted the MoU “offered the only viable pathway towards enduring peace in the region”. On his part, President Pezeshkian appreciated Pakistan’s “consistent diplomatic efforts for regional peace and security”, according to PMO. He also underscored the enduring strength of Pakistan-Iran relations, rooted in centuries of shared history, culture, and faith and reaffirmed Tehran’s strong desire to further deepen cooperation across a wide range of sectors. The president reiterated the need to forge unity among the Muslim community to deal with contemporary challenges. PM Shehbaz extended an invitation to President Pezeshkian to undertake an official visit to Pakistan at his earliest convenience. The Iranian president also invited the prime minister to the forthcoming summit of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) in Tehran in December 2026. The meeting was attended by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi and Foreign Secretary Ambassador Amna Baloch, PMO said. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and other high officials were also present. Shehbaz meets Uzbek president In a meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stressed the importance of timely implementation of decisions taken at the leadership level, particularly in trade, investment, connectivity and economic cooperation, the PMO said. According to the PMO, the meeting between the two leaders took place on the sidelines of the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek. Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, Communications Minister Aleem Khan and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar were also present. “The prime minister stressed the importance of timely implementation of decisions taken at the leadership level, particularly in trade, investment, connectivity and economic cooperation,” it said. PM Shehbaz reiterated the shared objective of increasing bilateral trade to $2 billion by 2029 and called for effective implementation of the expanded Preferential Trade Agreement, greater business-to-business engagement and promotion of mutually beneficial joint ventures, the PMO added. While highlighting regional connectivity as a shared strategic priority, the prime minister underscored the transformative potential of the Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan Railway in linking Central and South Asia and facilitating Uzbekistan’s access to Pakistan’s seaports. “He emphasised early progress on the Joint Feasibility Study and greater utilisation of existing multimodal transport corridors,” the PMO said, adding that “the prime minister also reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to facilitate Uzbek trade through its ports and transport infrastructure.” During the meeting, the two sides discussed further strengthening cooperation in industry, agriculture, pharmaceuticals, textiles, mining, digital technologies, education, culture, defence and security. “The prime minister also supported enhanced air connectivity, including progress towards direct Tashkent-Karachi flights.” The prime minister appreciated Uzbekistan’s support for Pakistan’s forthcoming chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State and expressed the desire to work closely with Uzbekistan on regional security, connectivity, trade and sustainable development, the PMO stated. “PM Shehbaz also emphasised continued cooperation within ECO and other multilateral forums.” “The prime minister reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its strategic partnership with Uzbekistan and translating the excellent political relationship into tangible economic benefits for the peoples of both countries,” the PMO concluded. PM arrives in Kyrgyzstan Adylbek Kasymaliev, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, welcomed PM Shehbaz upon his arrival at Manas International Airport, the government’s official account on social media platform X stated . Announcing the premier’s departure, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said he would address the SCO summit and “present Pakistan’s stance on various regional and global issues”. It added that Minister of Commerce Jam Kamal Khan, Minister of Communications Abdul Aleem Khan, and Minister of Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar were accompanying PM Shehbaz. During the visit, Pakistan is set to assume the chairmanship of the SCO’s Council of Heads of State for 2026–27, with next year’s CHS summit to be hosted by Islamabad. Earlier in the day, the Foreign Office had issued a statement on PM Shehbaz’s visit, saying that it would include participation in the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting, as well as bilateral engagements in the Kyrgyz Republic. “During his stay in Bishkek, the prime minister will participate in the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State and the SCO Plus Summit,” the statement said. “The prime minister will also assume Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-2027,” it said, adding that he would also hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of the participating countries on the sidelines. PM Shehbaz will also participate in the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games on Aug 31, the statement said. It added that on Sept 2, the prime minister would hold bilateral discussions with the Kyrgyz president on the “entire spectrum of Pakistan-Kyrgyzstan relations”. “The two sides will comprehensively review Pakistan-Kyrgyzstan relations and discuss ways to further deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, energy, regional connectivity, education, tourism, and people-to-people exchanges,” it said. “The leaders will also exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest and cooperation at regional and multilateral fora,” it added. “Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan enjoy warm and fraternal relations, rooted in shared history, faith and cultural affinity, as well as common aspirations for peace, connectivity and prosperity in Central and South Asia,” the FO said. “The forthcoming visit will provide an important opportunity to consolidate the momentum generated by recent high-level exchanges, translate political goodwill into enhanced practical cooperation, and further strengthen the enduring partnership between Pakistan and the Kyrgyz Republic,” the statement concluded. Deputy PM Ishaq Dar will join the Pakistani delegation in Bishkek for the SCO Council of Heads of State Meeting and the SCO Plus Summit, FO said in a separate update. Dar will accompany PM Shehbaz during his engagements in Bishkek, including bilateral discussions with President Sadyr Zhaparov on 2 September on Pakistan–Kyrgyzstan relations and ways to further strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

Court hands Hindu woman to family after alleged forced conversion and marriage. LAHORE: A 21-year-old Hindu woman from Sanghar district in Sindh, who was allegedly lured into a relationship and persuaded to convert to Islam by a man from Gujranwala in Punjab, was handed back into her family’s custody after a judicial magistrate on Monday rejected a police request to shift her to a shelter home. The woman went missing from her hometown. Sanghar police registered an FIR on the complaint of her brother. The complainant alleged that CCTV footage from a camera installed at their residence showed some unidentified persons forcibly taking his sister, along with valuables and mobile phones, during the night between August 23 and 24. Her family alleged that she was lured away and taken to Gujranwala, where she was pressured to convert to Islam and marry a local man, who was already married. Officials from the Sindh Home Department informed their counterparts in Punjab about the FIR and sought assistance in recovering the woman. Acting on the information, Eminabad police in Gujranwala recovered the woman and produced her before a judicial magistrate on Monday. During the proceedings, the investigating officer also filed an application requesting the magistrate to send the woman to Darul Aman for “safe custody”, claiming that she was unwilling to go with her parents. However, her lawyers — Asad Jamal and Kheta Ram — opposed the police request, telling the court that she was, in fact, willing to return to her parents’ home with her real brother, who was present in court. They said the woman also wanted to record her statement. The magistrate ordered that the woman’s statement be recorded directly. In her statement, given on oath, she said she wished to go with her brother to her parents’ home in of her own free will and consent. She added that she faced no threat to her life and was under no pressure while recording her statement. In his order, the magistrate ruled that, in view of the woman’s recorded statement, the police request to send her to Darul Aman “is hereby turned down”. The magistrate allowed her to go with her brother, entrusting him with her safe custody and transportation back to her parents’ home in Sanghar. Personnel from Sanghar police station in Sindh were also present in court.

PPP chairman Bilawal refutes reports of his engagement, wedding. PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari, the man at the centre of engagement and wedding rumours , himself refuted the reports on Monday. “Social media has gotten my baat pakki , engagement and wedding done. I clarify that nothing as such has taken place; neither do I know any Princess Gloria,” the Bhutto scion said in a video statement. He added, “If any such decision about my life is made, the announcement will come from my family. Till then, focus on the real issues and ignore the social media fuss.” Bilawal contended that the social media ruckus was made to “distract the public’s attention from the real issues”. He then turned his attention towards the tragic fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in Islamabad that claimed the lives of 14 infants . “A minister, who wants to become the Gorbachev of Pakistan and divide our country into 30 pieces, cannot manage one hospital himself,” he claimed, apparently comparing Health Minister Mustafa Kamal to the last leader of the Soviet Union until it dissolved in 1991. Kamal belongs to the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), which has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh. The PPP, which rules the province, opposes this strongly. “At a time when a Lahore minister is telling the businessmen of Lahore, ‘Make provinces and govern them’, at a time when the Sindh Assembly has taken a courageous stance and asserted that such discussions cannot take place on the streets or at business forums,” Bilawal said. The PPP chief said that any such discussions and decisions must be taken in the Sindh Assembly, noting it was the first province to join Pakistan. Bilawal’s clarification video comes after reports circulated that the PPP chairman — the son of President Asif Ali Zardari and ex-premier Benazir Bhutto — was preparing to marry into a European family. The reports claimed that President Asif Ali Zardari had travelled to Liechtenstein — a small sovereign state between Switzerland and Austria — to discuss and set a date for his son’s wedding. There were also claims that Bilawal’s prospective bride was a former Austrian princess. On August 27, the Presidency posted on X that Zardari “has proceeded abroad on a private visit”, but did not share any further details.

NA, Senate committees question probe into deadly Pims fire. ISLAMABAD: Standing committees of both houses of parliament on Monday questioned the probe into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) fire that killed 14 infants , raising concerns over incomplete CCTV footage and the disputed number of infants present in the nursery. The inquiry committee established to investigate the deadly hospital fire had submitted its interim report to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday, after which the premier ordered the suspension of and criminal action against eight officials. Furthermore, the health ministry accepted the resignation of Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) Chairman Dr Riaz Shahbaz Janjua. In his resignation, Dr Janjua said that some developments and circumstances had affected the autonomy of the authority. He said that, under the prevailing circumstances, it was not possible for him to perform his responsibilities independently and effectively. Dr Janjua was appointed as a member of the IHRA board in October 2024. He was then unanimously elected as its chairman. In his resignation letter, he said he had worked hard despite having limited human resources. NA committee questions executive director appointment The National Assembly Standing Committee on Health, chaired by MNA Mahesh Kumar Malani, was not satisfied with the report prepared by the inquiry committee. “We have called this meeting regarding the Pims tragedy because we are not satisfied with the report of the committee constituted by the prime minister,” Malani said. He also directed the media not to record videos of the committee proceedings. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, however, defended the inquiry and invited members to raise their objections. Shazia Soomro questioned why the NA’s standing committee had not been properly briefed about the circumstances of the incident. “We visited the site but proper briefing was not given, due to which we don’t have a clear picture,” she said. Malani pointed out that the CCTV footage was incomplete and called for the complete footage to be presented. He said the missing footage from inside the nursery was very important, adding that, in the available footage, a nurse could be seen entering the nursery, but it did not show what happened inside. Malani also questioned the responses given by the former executive director (ED) of Pims, saying that the officer had failed to provide satisfactory answers. The committee was told that nurses said they were looking after the babies and had not noticed the source of the spark. The members also raised questions about the possible role of oxygen in the incident. Committee Chairman Malani sought technical evidence regarding the fire and blast. Malani demanded a report from the biomedical engineering department and asked when the nursery’s last inspection had been conducted. He also claimed that the inquiry committee had failed to verify the exact number of babies present in the nursery at the time of the incident, citing some media reports that there were 15 babies in the ward. The chair stressed that the standing committee had representation from all political parties and that its members would examine the matter beyond party lines. Kamal said the prime minister had constituted the inquiry committee at around 4pm on the day of the incident. “Four people were included in the [inquiry] committee,” he said, adding that the health ministry had not conducted a separate investigation after the inquiry committee submitted its report. The standing committee also raised serious questions over the appointment of the new ED of Pims. Malani questioned whether a pathologist could effectively run the country’s largest public-sector hospital. He also said that the Pims Act stipulated that the ED should be appointed from within Pims. Kamal explained that the appointment had been made by the Prime Minister’s Office and that a relaxation of the relevant legal provision had been granted. However, he said, “the new ED will not be able to work”. Kamal has been vocal about his belief that government employees cannot run departments. At the standing committee meeting, MNA Aalia Kamran also expressed reservations about the inquiry process, saying no one had politically accepted responsibility for the tragedy. Senate committee condemns lack of safety reports The Senate Standing Committee on Health, under the chairmanship of Senator Amir Waliuddin Chishti, reviewed the adequacy of medical, paediatric and emergency care, fire safety arrangements, administrative and systemic deficiencies, accountability measures, patient safety and measures to prevent such incidents in the future. The meeting was attended by Senators Syed Masroor Ahsan, Rubina Khalid, Nadeem Ahmed Bhutto and Nasir Mehmood, while Senator Shahzaib Durrani participated through a Zoom link. MNA Sabeen Ghauri also attended the meeting as a special invitee. The committee visited the Pims nursery and raised serious concerns over the absence of fire alarms and the reported closure of emergency exits. Members also expressed displeasure over construction materials placed outside the labour room, observing that such obstructions could pose serious risks to patients and staff. The chairman directed the Pims administration to immediately remove all materials creating hurdles in hospital wards and access points. During a detailed briefing, the Pims administration stated that the situation had been managed within a few minutes. However, committee members questioned the availability of duty staff, including doctors, at the time of the incident and observed that the presence of adequate staff could potentially have helped evacuate and save the infants. Health Minister Kamal informed the committee that, according to the preliminary inquiry report, the fire spread within approximately 120 seconds, resulting in the tragic loss of lives. He also informed the committee of an earlier fire incident at the Pims nursing hostel in July 2026 , which he said he had only learned about after the Wednesday fire. The Senate committee unanimously resolved to scrutinise the inquiry committee’s report and called for a comprehensive, impartial and technically sound investigation into the incident. Members observed that established fire safety protocols had not been adequately followed and that no regular fire drills had been conducted. They added that the relevant authorities had failed to carry out the necessary inspection visits. The committee emphasised the need to clearly separate administrative and clinical responsibilities in public hospitals. Members expressed concern over officials holding multiple additional charges and doctors being assigned administrative responsibilities, stressing that hospital administration should be managed by qualified professionals with relevant expertise. Members asked whether there was a well-maintained register tracking safety reports. The committee also questioned the IHRA over the reported absence of inspection visits to Pims over the last two years. Members raised concerns over the composition and functioning of the IHRA board, while the Senate committee chairman directed Kamal to review and reform the regulatory mechanism and board composition. The committee also expressed serious dissatisfaction over the performance and coordination of the relevant authorities, including the Capital Development Authority (CDA), rescue authorities, civil defence, Pims administration and IHRA. The committee further said that legislation would be enacted to prevent such incidents in the future.

Seven players, including Rizwan and Imam, dropped after second Test defeat in England: PCB. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Monday announced the release of seven Test squad members, including Mohammad Rizwan, Imamul Haq and Salman Ali Agha, during the ongoing series against England. The cricket board’s decision came after Pakistan suffered a thumping 194-run defeat to England in the second Test at Lord’s. With the victory, the hosts took an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match Test series, after the visitors also suffered an innings-and-103-run thrashing in the first Test at Headingley. According to a press release, Rizwan, Imam, Agha, along with Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad, have been released from the squad. The PCB also named seven replacements, including “five uncapped players at Test level and two capped players”. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, who have played eight and two Tests, respectively, have been called up to the Test squad. Among the five uncapped players are left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, who has represented Pakistan in three ODIs and four T20Is; left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Imran Jr.; wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig, who was named player of the tournament in the 2025-26 Quaid-i-Azam Trophy; and right-arm pace-bowling all-rounders Mohammad Imran (also known as Imran Randhawa) and Razaullah. “The players will join the Pakistan squad ahead of the third Test against England,” the release said. The third and final match of the series is scheduled for September 9 in Birmingham. Additionally, Test head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul have also been relieved of their duties, the release said, adding that white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke will replace them on the backroom staff. Updated Test squad for Birmingham Test: Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ali, Muhammad Imran, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wicket-keeper), Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicket-keeper) Saim Ayub, Sajid Khan, Saud Shakeel, Shan Masood and Ubaid Shah

Makkah Defence Alliance to be institutionalised, Pakistan to head secretariat for 3 years: FO. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to further institutionalise their cooperation under the Makkah Agreement to strengthen collective deterrence and defence, with the alliance’s secretariat to be initially headed by Pakistan for three years, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday. The decision was taken at the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Agreement, held in Istanbul. Foreign and defence ministers of the three countries, as well as top military officials, attended the meeting in Istanbul’s Ciragan Palace. Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif represented Pakistan. According to the FO, a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. The secretariat will initially be headed by a secretary general from Pakistan for a period of three years. The three countries also agreed to take steps to further institutionalise their cooperation in a manner that would enhance their solidarity, ensure the credibility and effectiveness of their collective deterrence and defence, and contribute to regional efforts and cooperative security towards a just, inclusive and lasting peace. “Acting with a sense of regional ownership, the three countries reiterate their determination to work together within the framework of the Makkah Agreement to achieve sustainable peace and stability in their region. To that end, they will continue to support efforts towards de-escalation and restraint to encourage peaceful resolution of crises,” added the FO statement. The three countries will also seek to strengthen their defence capabilities and the cohesion of their armed forces through joint activities, robust defence industry cooperation, and joint technology development and production, the FO said. “Through the institutionalised and resolute implementation of the Makkah Agreement, the three countries will provide essential contributions to regional peace and stability,” it added. ‘Makkah Defence Alliance’ Earlier, Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said that the tripartite agreement between Ankara, Islamabad and Riyadh will be known as “Makkah Defence Alliance”, with its first secretary general to be from Pakistan. He made the announcement while addressing a press conference following the first meeting of the committee, established under the agreement. In his press conference, Fidan noted that his country hosted the first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee on Monday. He said the meeting was held “in relation to the concrete steps that are going to be taken for the implementation of the agreement” and an exchange of views was held for that purpose. “As of today, we have started the process of establishing the institutional structure of the alliance,” Fidan said, announcing that the agreement’s official name will be “Makkah Defence Alliance”. “There is a secretariat that has been established in Riyadh, and the first secretary general will be appointed amongst our Pakistani brothers,” he said. He said that during the meeting, decisions were taken on “how and when to begin institutionalisation and all our brothers expressed views during the meeting”. Fidan hoped that decisions taken in the meeting will yield “excellent results”. “For the future of a secure, stable and prosperous region, this alliance is based on international principles such as respecting the sovereignty of other states, territorial integrity and not intervening in internal affairs,” he said, adding that the alliance was not against any country. He maintained that the alliance was “open for the partnership and participation of any other country”. However, Fidan stressed that there were “some conditions, rules and standards”, adding that the alliance’s nature was such that it was “expected to expand”. Stressing the need for institutionalisation of the alliance, he said: “If an ally wants to join, the alliance should be functional in a proper manner by then.” He added that the alliance did not “eliminate our countries’ responsibilities to other agreements or alliances”. Fidan hoped that with Monday’s meeting, the three countries had demonstrated readiness to take responsibility for the security and stability of the region. “We will closely cooperate with friendly countries, and we will continue coordinating our efforts,” he said. Fidan also noted that the lack of “alliances and trust” between regional countries had given rise to security problems. The joint defence pact, signed on August 7, empowers the member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. CDF Munir meets Saudi defence minister Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on the sidelines of the first meeting of the Strategic Political Defence Committee of the Makkah Defence Alliance, according to a post on his X account. He said that he and Field Marshal Munir reviewed the potential for military and defence cooperation between Islamabad and Riyadh and “discussed developments in the regional situation and the efforts being made in response to them”. Inaugural meeting of ‘Makkah Defence Alliance’ The Foreign Office (FO) shared pictures from the tripartite meeting, which was attended by FM Dar, Asif and CDF Munir. DPM Dar, in a post on X, termed it a “great inaugural meeting”. According to Anadolu Agency , Fidan, National Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu represented Turkiye at the meeting. Representing Saudi Arabia, FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan, Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Chief of General Staff General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili attended the meeting. Anadolu Agency also shared a video showing the participants seated in a hall, with Fidan seated in the middle. The clip showed the Turkish FM greeting Dar, CDF Munir and others at the venue. In a statement issued on Sunday, FO said Pakistan’s participation in the meeting signifies its “historic bonds of friendship with the brotherly countries of Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, as well as its desire for lasting regional peace and stability”. The maiden ministerial meeting under the Makkah pact is being seen as the first step towards establishing a framework for trilateral strategic and defence cooperation. Bilateral meetings Ahead of the trilateral pact’s inaugural moot, the signatories held multiple bilateral meetings in Istanbul. CDF Munir met Turkish National Defence Minister Yaşar Güler ahead of the first meeting under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Istanbul. In a post on the social media platform X, the Turkish Ministry of National Defence shared a video of CDF Munir meeting Güler. The Turkish minister also held a separate meeting with Asif, with Chief of General Staff General Selçuk Bayraktaroğlu in attendance. According to Radio Pakistan , Asif and the Turkish leadership agreed to enhance joint defence cooperation in the region. Meanwhile, Turkiye’s foreign minister met his Saudi counterpart on the margins of the trilateral moot. Fidan had already held a meeting with Dar on Sunday. Both the deputy premier and the army chief had arrived in Turkiye a day earlier. After concluding his visit to Istanbul, Dar departed for Bishkek alongside the Turkish foreign and defence ministers, FO said. He will join Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the Pakistani delegation for the SCO Council of Heads of State Meeting and the SCO Plus Summit.

Peace march in AJK's Sudhnoti demands early elections, end to blockades. MUZAFFARABAD: A large number of people from different walks of life took part in a peace march on Monday in Palandri, the district headquarters of Sudhnoti in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), calling for an end to unrest and blockades and immediate elections in seven constituencies of Poonch and Sudhnoti. Recent elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were held in phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10. Organised by the Public Alliance Forum Sudhnoti, the march began at Kotli Chowk and passed through various streets before culminating in a public gathering at Kutchery Chowk. The participants carried AJK and Pakistani flags, with banners bearing slogans such as “This homeland is ours, we are its guardians”, “Unrest in the state is unacceptable”, “Lawlessness in the state is unacceptable” and “What do we want? Peace!” Representatives of the PML-N, PPP, Muslim Conference, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Party, Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party and PTI, alongside traders, lawyers, transporters, civil society representatives, educationists and ex-servicemen, addressed the gathering. In a joint declaration, the participants urged the governments of Pakistan and AJK to immediately hold elections in the seven constituencies of Poonch and Sudhnoti where polling could not take place during the recent AJK elections due to the law and order situation. They also called for the immediate removal of blockades by both the government and protesters, whether inside AJK or at entry points into Pakistan, to ease the public’s difficulties in travelling and obtaining essential goods. The participants additionally demanded the restoration of travel and educational facilities, particularly in Sudhnoti and Poonch; the immediate restoration of internet services across AJK; and uninterrupted supplies of food and other essential commodities from Pakistan. They said restrictions on the movement of these goods had compounded the difficulties faced by the people. It also called for adequate supplies of wheat to flour mills to ensure the regular distribution of flour, uninterrupted availability of petrol and hassle-free processing of documents required by people travelling abroad. Participants also expressed concern over rumours of the possible relocation of educational and administrative institutions from Rawalakot. They demanded that the “endless sacrifices” made by the “brave, courageous and patriotic people” of the region for the Kashmir freedom movement and the “completion of Pakistan” should not be overlooked, urging the authorities to avoid any such step. It reiterated that no one could weaken the “everlasting bond” between Kashmiris and Pakistan and that a strong and stable Pakistan was the guarantor of the freedom movement, while AJK served as a “strong defence shield” for Pakistan. “Promoting instability in the region will not be allowed,” the participants declared. The peace march also congratulated the government of Pakistan and the armed forces for what it described as their role in promoting global peace. The PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani was elected as AJK PM after being sworn in last Friday. His sole contender was PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmed Abbasi, who bagged 14 votes in the contest for the top office. The third phase of polling was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. The AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation. In the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party also joined hands with the PML-N . As for the reserved seats, the PML-N bagged six and the PPP two. The PPP alleged widespread rigging and irregularities in the elections.

Opposition walks out as Punjab Assembly passes controversial Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill 2026. LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Monday passed the controversial Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026, despite objections and a full walkout by opposition lawmakers. The session saw heated exchanges between government members and the opposition, centred on a debate between Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan and Opposition Leader Moin Riaz Qureshi over the legal and constitutional implications of the new legislation. Addressing the house, Speaker Khan issued a ruling confirming that the bill could legally be placed on the agenda, citing Article 142 of the Constitution concerning criminal-law jurisdiction. Defending the move, the speaker referred to his personal experiences from the 1990s, recalling how terrorism claimed more than 100,000 lives in Pakistan, including those of high-profile figures such as Col (retd) Shuja Khanzada and Captain Mubeen, and led to attacks on places of worship such as Data Darbar. He argued that, in the past, terrorists often walked free due to a lack of witness protection and physical security. He noted that even democratic nations such as the US had established “faceless” or anonymous courts to deal with extreme terror threats, urging the opposition to propose constructive amendments rather than block the bill. However, Qureshi fiercely condemned the law, labelling it “draconian” and calling it a “bill to crush the citizens of Punjab”. He accused the ruling government of introducing the amendment to target political rivals, particularly PTI leaders and activists, much like previous defamation and National Accountability Bureau laws. He raised concerns over a provision under which a Grade-20 designated official would have the authority to advise the chief justice of the Lahore High Court on whether cases should be classified as “special security cases”. Joining the debate, opposition lawmaker Ahmar Rashid Bhatti read out on the floor of the House an opinion column he had written for a daily newspaper, comparing the proposed law to a 1909 British colonial-era act that was opposed by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan. He warned that allowing the identities and voices of judges, prosecutors, defence lawyers and witnesses to be concealed or altered would violate Article 10-A of the Constitution, which guarantees the fundamental right to a fair and transparent trial. Following the intense debate, opposition members chanted slogans against the bill and walked out of the hall. As they exited, lawmaker Waqas Mann pointed out a lack of quorum, but the treasury benches successfully rallied enough members to maintain the quorum. With the opposition absent, their proposed amendments were rejected, and the House voted to approve the Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Anti-Terrorism (Punjab Amendment) Bill 2026 The bill seeks to insert a new Section 21AAA into the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, creating a “special security case” mechanism for cases in which participants are considered to require extraordinary protection. Under the proposed law, a designated authority — an officer of at least BS-20 whose identity would itself remain confidential — could declare a case or a class of cases a special security case. At the authority’s request, the chief justice of the Lahore High Court would assign the case to an Anti-Terrorism Court judge. The bill also proposes that the identities of judges, public prosecutors, defence counsel, police officers, witnesses and other persons involved in such proceedings “shall not be disclosed”. Judicial orders would carry official titles instead of the judges’ names, while witnesses would be identified through codes issued by the designated authority. The proceedings could be held at secure premises or conducted through video links, including from prisons. The proposed provision would also allow the government to adopt other security measures it considers appropriate. An accused person would not be able to challenge the constitution of the tribunal, seek the recusal of a judge or effectively question the judge’s independence if the judge’s identity remained concealed. Under the existing anti-terrorism act, the trial record is required to be transmitted to the high court, while the accused is entitled to a copy of the judgment. However, keeping the record sealed with both the chief justice and the designated authority could make appellate scrutiny difficult. The proposed provision also gives the designated authority a role in selecting prosecutors. The prosecutor general would provide a panel of five public prosecutors, from which the designated authority would assign one to the case. Another contentious provision allows the regime to be applied to a “class of cases”, rather than requiring a case-by-case judicial determination. The bill’s “notwithstanding” clause, which gives the proposed provision effect over the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Code of Criminal Procedure, has also been flagged as a potential source of conflict with federal legislation and constitutional provisions.

Chinese town emerges as world’s guitar capital. ZHENG’AN: It doesn’t take long to gue­ss the main industry of the Chinese town of Zheng’an. A giant guitar sculpture dominates the central square, guitar murals adorn walls and pavements and even the rubbish bins are shaped like guitars. This corner of the southwest province of Guizhou produces one in every seven of the instruments sold worldwide. A decade ago, it had no guitar-making industry to speak of at all. There are hundreds of specialised manufacturing towns in China, producing items ranging from bicycles to socks. But the speed and scale of Zheng’an’s rise make it an example of the impact of China’s industrial strategy when a combination of local and central government investment is deployed to maximise favourable local conditions. For years, the town’s working-age residents left to find employment in factories in Guangdong, southern China’s manufacturing hub. Among them was Zheng Chuanjiu, who eventually started his own guitar-making business in the provincial capital Guangzhou. “The company was doing pretty well at that time and most of our staff in Guangzhou were also our fellow villagers from Zheng’an,” the founder of Shenqu Guitar said. In 2012, Zheng’an local authorities rolled out an initiative called “return the phoenix to the nest”, to encourage skilled migrant workers to return home and start businesses. “The county officials reached out to us. They wanted us to come back and develop the industry,” Zheng said. Shenqu became the first guitar manufacturer to settle in Zheng’an’s new economic zone. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

'Technical fault': Driverless car crashes into police van in Islamabad. KARACHI: A video clip went viral on social media after a remote-controlled car crashed into a police van in Islamabad, reportedly due to a “technical fault” caused by an internet disruption. On Sunday, journalist Muhammad Aalijah uploaded a video on his official social media account showing him seated in the front passenger seat of a car at Islamabad’s D-Chowk, which appeared to be operated using a remote-control device. As Aalijah explains the car’s features and it moves forward, the steering wheel, controlled remotely by an operator, suddenly goes out of control. The car consequently bumps into a police van parked along the road. The video also shows Aalijah pulling the handbrake in an attempt to prevent the car from hitting the police van, but his efforts prove futile. Since being uploaded, the video has been widely circulated on social media, with users adding witty captions to the footage. When contacted, Aalijah told Dawn that he had been asked by technology enthusiast Ehsan Zafar of Abbottabad to report on his tech-based automated-driving innovation. “Everything was fine until a technical fault occurred due to an internet disruption, causing the car to go out of control and crash into a police vehicle,” he said. Aalijah explained that the car was controlled remotely over the internet and that a sudden loss of connection caused it to go out of control. In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah said his intention in making the video was “never to defame or target this young man”, who owned and operated the car. “The sole purpose was to raise awareness and urge people to remain cautious until any new experiment or technology has been thoroughly tested, proven safe and established as a complete success,” he said. “This was a message of caution, not an attempt to discredit anyone.” Sharing the video online, Aalijah said the car’s system was not yet “completely safe and reliable”. “The vehicle was being operated through satellite and internet connections, but during external control, it went out of control as soon as the internet connection was disconnected and collided with a police vehicle,” he wrote. The incident occurred in a high-security area with very little traffic. “If the same situation had occurred on a busy road, the consequences could have been extremely dangerous, even fatal,” he said. “This video is not criticism; it is a responsible effort to raise awareness and issue a warning — by all means, experiment, but ensure safety first,” he added. Self-driving memes take on a life of their own Meanwhile, the video has been widely shared on social media, with some users appreciating the journalist’s efforts to promote local talent, while others have responded with amusing remarks. “Certainly, there is no shortage of talent in Pakistan,” a user wrote, quoting Aalijah in a jibe. An internet user added that even AI panics in Pakistan when it sees the cops. Another user advised the car’s owner and tech innovator not to give up. “Funny for some, maybe, but I see a great effort. It failed today; yes, hiccups happen, but I know this young Pakistani will one day have a perfect solution.” Noting the huge public attention, a user said the video clip had the potential to become the next “international meme”.

Govt cuts arms licence issuance by over 90pc. • Only 5,700 non-prohibited-bore arms licences issued in 13 months, Senate body told • Tallal Chaudhry says 60pc of those involved in terrorism incidents in KP and Balochistan were Afghan nationals ISLAMABAD: The federal government has cut the issuance of non-prohibited-bore arms licences by more than 90 per cent, with only 5,700 licences issued over the past 13 months under strict criteria, the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control was informed on Monday. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry told the committee, which met under the chairmanship of Senator Faisal Saleem Rehman, that more than 100,000 arms licences had previously been issued annually. He said a police character certificate was now mandatory to ensure that people with criminal records did not obtain licences. A parliamentarian’s recommendation was also required, with each National Assembly constituency limited to five recommendations per month. The minister added that prohibited-bore licences were issued strictly to entitled persons, including parliamentarians, judges, army and police officers, and recipients of national awards. Officials said there was no policy for issuing business-category arms licences in Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the former Fata. The ministry would brief the committee on the procedure for dealing with special cases. On visas for Afghan nationals, Mr Chaudhry said no visa was issued without due diligence and that extensions were granted on a case-by-case basis, mainly on humanitarian grounds for students and those requiring medical treatment. He said around one million Afghans had been issued visas over two years when relations with the neighbouring country were normal. The National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) informed the committee that Afghan visa applications were processed under 18 categories handled by the Ministry of Interior and four by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, mainly for businesspeople and students. However, delays occurred due to security clearances. Senator Talha Mahmood said there should be some relaxation in the visa policy for businessmen and students. Mr Chaudhry told the committee that 60 per cent of those involved in terrorism incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan were Afghan nationals. “Afghanistan is our neighbour but its intentions are not right,” he said. He ad­­ded that Afghan nationals had also been involved in terrorism incidents in Islam­abad and in the murder of trader Aamir. The committee was informed that the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) does not routinely check passengers’ mobile phones or social media accounts at airports. “We do not check anyone’s mobile phone at the airport. Only those about whom we have information regarding human smuggling are checked. We also do not check the social media of any passenger,” an FIA official said. Mr Chaudhry, without naming any country, said, “When I went abroad with my family, all of our social media was checked.” The committee was briefed on an intelligence-based Sindh Police operation in District Shikarpur that resulted in the recovery of minor girl Huram Saeed Pathan, who was kidnapped from Karachi on March 28, 2026, and another trafficked victim, Jennifer Amir. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026
