Japan, Belgium defense chiefs agree to deepen security ties. TOKYO, Aug. 31 (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and his Belgian counterpart, Theo Francken, at a meeting in Tokyo on Monday agreed to deepen security cooperation between their countries. Koizumi welcomed Belgium's first assignment of a defense attache to its embassy in Tokyo, saying this is highly significant as the security in the Euro-Atlantic region and that in the Indo-Pacific region are becoming increasingly inseparable. The two ministers exchanged views on regional developments and confirmed cooperation to maintain a free and open international order based on the rule of law. Francken, who also serves as Belgium's trade minister, expressed his eagerness to strengthen defense industry cooperation with Japan.

Philippine manufacturing surges to near-decade high in August as output, orders accelerate. Philippine manufacturing activity accelerated sharply in August, with factory conditions improving at their strongest pace in nearly a decade as production growth hit its fastest rate since 2016 amid stronger demand. In a report on Tuesday, Sept. 1, S&P Global said its Philippines manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) climbed to 54.9 in August from 51.8 in July, marking the fourth consecutive monthly increase and the strongest improvement in the health of the sector since December 2016. A PMI reading above 50 indicates an overall improvement in manufacturing conditions compared with the previous month, while a reading below 50 signals a deterioration. “The Filipino manufacturing sector continued to build momentum in August, moving on from the flat performance seen in the previous quarter, when activity was affected by the conflict in the Middle East. Encouragingly, production rose at its fastest pace since 2016, helped by stronger demand conditions,” S&P Global Market Intelligence economist Maryam Baluch said in a statement. Manufacturing output rose substantially during the month, with the pace of growth accelerating from July to its fastest since December 2016. Firms attributed the increase to stronger underlying demand and greater production efficiency. Inflows of new work also rose at the fastest rate in six months, supported by new product and model launches, higher repeat business, and a broader customer base. International demand likewise improved, with new export orders rising for the first time in six months. The stronger order books prompted manufacturers to step up purchasing activity, which expanded at a six-month high. Stocks of purchases also increased for the first time since February despite a deterioration in supplier performance. “Firms responded by increasing both purchasing and hiring to keep up with greater production needs. At the same time, cost pressures eased, and confidence about the year ahead improved to a 21-month high,” Baluch said. Manufacturers also increased staffing levels for the first time in five months. Although the increase was modest, the pace of job creation was the strongest in 21 months. Cost pressures, meanwhile, eased despite firms continuing to report higher expenses for energy, raw materials, and logistics. Input cost inflation slowed notably from July, while output charges increased at the weakest pace in the current six-month period of inflation. Business confidence also strengthened to its highest level since November 2024, as manufacturers expecting higher output over the next 12 months cited expansion plans, new product lines, stronger order inflows, and expectations of attracting new customers. S&P Global’s Philippines manufacturing PMI is compiled from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers at a panel of around 400 manufacturers. Data for the August survey were collected from Aug. 12 to 24. - Danielle T. Bayani

LTFRB warns PUV drivers vs road bullying, summons bus operator. The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) warned operators and drivers of passenger buses and other big motor vehicles to refrain from bullying smaller ones following a viral counterflow video which the agency described as dangerous and disrespectful. Acting LTFRB chairman Greg G. Pua, Jr. was referring to the overtaking incident involving a bus of the Victory Liner that forced a motorcycle rider to stop and pull over alongside the road. “Roads are not the place of bullying of big motor vehicles to smaller ones, we will not allow that and those who would dare do that in the public transportation sector will suffer consequences,” said Pua. What made it dangerous is that the overtaking and counterflowing happened on the blind or curved side of the road, which forced a rider to pull over alongside the road. Pua said the entire incident was captured on the video which served as the basis for the show cause order (SCO) issuance when the LTFRB monitored it on social media. In the SCO, the LTFRB asked the bus operator to explain in writing why its Certificate of Public Convenience (CPC) should not be suspended or cancelled over the dangerous driving behavior of one of its drivers. The same document stated that the passenger bus endangered road users and the act committed by the driver falls under failure to provide safe and convenient public transportation service. The bus firm is also facing an administrative case of employing a reckless driver, according to Pua. The hearing of the case is on September 10. Pua reminded public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers to behave and always observe road courtesy and discipline in the interest of the safety of all road users. “Road crashes are preventable and one of the key factors is discipline and respect to all fellow road users. On the part of the LTFRB, we will pursue accountability against those who would defy that,” said Pua.

P200-M flood control infrastructure to protect thousands living in riverside communities in Agusan del Sur. BUTUAN CITY – Thousands of riverside community folks may now have some measure of security whenever heavy rains come after two of Gibong River Bank flood control infrastructure worth almost P200 million in Las Navas and La Suerte, both in Prosperidad town, Agusan del Sur province, recently became operational. These two flood control protection infrastructure are eagerly anticipated projects for the thousands of community folks, especially farmers who frequently experience anxiety and worry during bad weather conditions that causes flood. The construction of Gibong River Bank slope protection structure along Barangay Las Navas is already 96.68 percent complete, and only the remaining works of parapet and concrete slabs are being undertaken by the Agusan del Sur 1st District Engineering Office (DEO) of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH-1st District DEO). “This 186.0m length Las Navas project is hitting its timeline of completion by the end of this month of September,” said DPWH 13 Assistant Regional Director (ARD) Engr. Vincent Roderick “Bong” M. Acebes, in an interview with The Manila Bulletin on Tuesday, Sept. 1. He said round-the-clock ground works are being undertaken by the engineers and personnel of the 1st District DEO and assigned contractor to hit their target timeline of completion. “The completion of Las Navas project is tentatively by the end of this month (September),” ARD Acebes pointed out. On the other hand, the 182.4m length construction of flood control structure in La Suerte area, also along Gibong River is already 100% complete, only on Thursday, Aug. 27, this year. These two flood control structures that started in the middle of 2025 was built by the DPWH to ensure the safety of residents and their properties from flooding, particularly farm lands in these areas, also said DPWH 13 Regional Director Sabeniano D. Caliao, Jr. He said the instruction of our DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon was to finish these projects to ensure the safety of our community folks and land properties of farmers, the DPWH 13 top official added. “It is a long-awaited project as raging flood waters forced our locals living along this giant Gibong River to leave and reside in a safer place. With the total completion of these flood control structures, they are now better protected and their safety is ensured,” also said Agusan del Sur solon Rep. Adolph Edward “Eddiebong” Plaza. Plaza expressed heartfelt gratitude to the DPWH for the completion of these projects in Sabang Gibong River Bank.

Iconic Burnham Lake in Baguio City is opened to public after P150-M rehab. BAGUIO CITY – Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) Operating Officer Mark Lapid led the opening of the P150-million worth of rehabilitation of the famous Burnham Lake, which is the first highlight of the 117th Baguio Day celebration, this morning, September 1. “Finally, it’s finished although there was a delay due to weather, but now it’s okay and we can start the rehabilitation of the children’s park and Rose Garden, so we can see the total rehabilitation of the entire Burnham Park. Apart from this, we also have a rehab on Session Road, which we will start after the Panagbenga celebration next year,” Lapid said. “Burnham Park is the heart of Baguio, when I was a kid, I used to go here for sightseeing, boating, biking, so it is an honor that we were given a position in the government and we were able to help beautify it” Mayor Benjamin Magalong said Burnham Lake and its surroundings have changed a lot. “The water is now clean because the lake was filled with rain, there is a walkway and there are new boats that will be placed here and coil and carp fish, to help with pollution.” He said that boat riders will no longer have difficulty boarding the boat because there is a deck for safety and they will have insurance from P350 to pay and will be required to use a safety vest, because the lake is deeper now He also said that the beauty of the lake now is that there is a pathway where you can jog in addition to the pathway that will be placed around Burnham Lake. “The big issue in this project is funding, fortunately TIEZA is there to help us beautify the entire Burnham Park. Hopefully before the end of this year, the Children Park and Rose Garden will also be finished,” Magalong said. According to Magalong, the beautification of our iconic Burnham Park, which is the main attraction in the Summer Capital, is a huge help for the city of Baguio. Magalong also announced that there are other projects in the pipeline, the initial P500-million water sewer system of Burnham Park and the rehabilitation of Session Road from TIEZA funds. Lapid was the guest honor and speaker at the Baguio Day celebration in recognition of his great contribution to the city’s tourism projects.

Agri technician dies in San Carlos flooding; 2 rescued, 60-year-old man missing. SAN CARLOS CITY, Pangasinan — A 28-year-old agricultural technician died after being pulled into extremely deep floodwaters while traversing a submerged road with three companions in Sitio Gulisan, Barangay Mabalbalino, this city, on August 31. Police said the incident occurred at around 3:50 p.m. as the group was making its way home along a concrete road submerged by floodwaters. Initial investigation showed that one of them accidentally stepped toward the edge of the road where the water was deeper, causing the group to lose their balance and pull one another into the deeper portion of the flooded area. The victim was subsequently retrieved by personnel of the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) and rushed to Virgen Milagrosa Medical Center. Despite efforts by medical personnel to revive him, the physician declared the victim dead. Meanwhile, a 27-year-old woman and a minor who were part of the group were rescued by concerned residents in the area. Search and rescue operations are continuing for another companion, a 60-year-old vendor, who remains missing as of the latest report. Authorities reminded residents to avoid crossing flooded roads.

PCG recovers body of Agana Bridge victim in Dagupan; search for 3 others continues. DAGUPAN CITY, Pangasinan — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) recovered on Monday, Aug. 31, the body of one of the five people who went missing after their vehicle plunged into the Tarlac River following the partial collapse of Agana Bridge in Tarlac City. The body was recovered in the waters off Barangay Pugaro , Dagupan City after a motorbanca operator reported seeing a floating cadaver at around noon. Coast Guard Station Dagupan immediately deployed a response team and conduct retrieval operations. Responders confirmed the sighting and recovered the body, which was brought to Barangay Poblacion Oeste and turned over to Dagupan City Police Station 5 for proper disposition. Tarlac City Mayor Susan Yap later confirmed that the recovered body was that of one of the victims of the Agana Bridge incident. The vehicle, carrying five occupants, plunged into the Tarlac River on Aug. 29 when the bridge partially collapsed. The incident triggered a search operation along the river and downstream areas. The PCG continues to search for the three other missing individuals, with teams scouring the Tarlac River and downstream areas in coordination with other government agencies.

Easy Japanese in focus as way to deliver info to foreigners. TOKYO, Sept. 1 (Jiji Press) -- Easy Japanese is in the spotlight as a way to disseminate information to foreigners in Japan, especially at the time of disasters such as a recent powerful earthquake that hit the southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto. According to a survey targeting foreigners living in Tokyo, 41.3 pct said they want to read information written in easy Japanese, higher than 35.9 pct seeking information in English. "It's probably because the nationalities of foreigners living in Japan have diversified, and fewer people are from English-speaking countries and regions," said Nobuko Inoue of Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation Tsunagari, which conducted the survey and works to promote and raise awareness about easy Japanese. The crux of giving out information in easy Japanese is to avoid using onomatopoeia, mimetic words, words adopted from foreign languages and ambiguous expressions, and to use short and clear sentences, according to the foundation. For example, "kyanseru," which derives from the English word cancel, can be replaced with "yameru" in easy Japanese. "Moraeru," meaning "you can get," can be used for "teikyo-suru," which means to provide. In Kumamoto, people from Southeast Asian countries, such as Vietnam and Indonesia, account for more than half of foreign residents. "We have many people whose native languages are not English," an official of the Kumamoto prefectural government's international affairs division said. "We are trying to provide information in easy Japanese rather than in English." On July 29, the day after the 7.1-magnitude earthquake, which measured up to 7, the highest level on Japan's seismic intensity scale, WizTry, an information technology company in Kumamoto, created a website (https://kumamoto-shien.jp/) to give affected people necessary information, which includes an easy Japanese page for foreign residents (https://kumamoto-shien.jp/yasashii). The page for foreigners says, for example: "Mizu wo kubaru basho ga arimasu. Okane wa irimasen," which means there are places where you can get water and no money is needed. WizTry President Kotaro Suematsu said he hopes the company's easy Japanese page will help foreigners who tend to be left out of information.

SINAG urges early water release from San Roque dam. PANGASINAN — San Roque Dam’s water elevation has climbed to 282.96 meters above sea level (masl) as of 5:00 a.m., Sept 1, prompting renewed calls for precautionary action as downstream communities remain vulnerable to flooding. Samahang Industriya ng Agrikultura (SINAG) Chairman Engr. Rosendo So had earlier urged dam authorities to begin controlled water releases when the reservoir was still at around 278 meters. “I ask San Roque Dam to release water at 278 level,” So said. With the current level already at 282.96 masl, or nearly five meters higher than the level cited by So, the appeal underscores the urgency of closely monitoring the reservoir and managing releases carefully to reduce potential downstream flood risks. The situation also recalls the massive flooding in 2009 following Typhoon Pepeng. On October 9, 2009, when San Roque Dam reached approximately 289.05 masl, all six spillway gates were reportedly opened, with discharge reaching about 5,072 cubic meters per second at one point. In 2009, after Typhoon Pepeng, Rosendo So and affected parties pursued legal action against National Power Corporation (NPC) and San Roque Power Corporation (SRPC) over the massive flooding and alleged improper/sudden release of water from San Roque Dam. With the dam now at 282.96 masl, authorities and downstream communities are urged to remain vigilant and closely monitor official dam and flood advisories.

Eruption of Sinabung volcano on Indonesia’s Sumatra island prompts higher alert. JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Mount Sinabung on Indonesia erupted Monday, spewing a column of black ash and smoke 3,500 meters (11,482 feet) from the top of the mountain into the sky over Sumatra island. There were no immediate reports of casualties, evacuations or disruptions to flights in the region. But residents, visitors and tourists were advised to refrain from activities in nearby villages in Karo district in North Sumatra province and areas within 6 kilometers (3.7 miles) of the summit. Roads, vehicles and buildings in several villages in Karo affected by the eruption were covered in gray ash. Local authorities distributed masks to residents to protect themselves. Officials raised the volcano alert level to “Watch,” the second-highest level for volcanic activity, which expanded the safe zone around the 2,600-meter (8,530-foot) mountain. “This eruption is considered an initial eruption, and it is possible that a larger eruption could occur,” Lana Saria, chief of Indonesia’s Geological Agency, said in a statement Monday. The agency previously recorded visual evidence of Mount Sinabung's increased activity in mid-August including dozens of earthquakes and expanded the recommended radius for public activities. About 30,000 people have been forced to leave their homes around Sinabung in the past few years because of volcanic activity. Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 280 million people with frequent seismic activity and Sinabung is among more than 120 active volcanoes. The country is prone to seismic upheaval due to its location on the Pacific “Ring of Fire,” an arc of volcanoes and fault lines encircling the Pacific Basin.

Eala set to draw big crowd at big stadium for US Open opener. Filipino fans are expected to troop to Louis Armstrong Stadium in New York on Tuesday evening, Sept. 1 (Wednesday morning, Sept. 2, Philippines time) as Alex Eala begins her US Open campaign against American qualifier Mary Stoiana. The match is slated not before 8:30 p.m. (8:30 a.m. Wednesday, Philippine time), immediately after the opening men’s singles clash between 2016 semifinalist Gael Monfils and Adolfo Vallejo, which is set for 7 p.m. (7 a.m. Wednesday, PH time). Organizers are expecting the 14,000-capacity stadium to be packed for Eala’s highly anticipated appearance. In an interview with Tennis Channel, tournament director Eric Butorac said organizers are embracing the growing fan support for Eala by putting her on the tournament’s second-largest stadium following the huge crowd that turned out for her exhibition match against Iva Jovic during Fan Week. “I don’t know if you guys caught any of that match, but it was electric in there. I mean, unbelievable,” sai Butorac. “We scheduled her first match at Louis Armstrong Stadium (because) we knew it had to be a major stadium. We thought that’s a great place to start. But I’ve already kind of monitored some of the secondary pricing, and that session is blowing up,” he added. As of Monday, Aug. 31, ticket prices at Ticketmaster for the night session at Louis Armstrong Stadium are as low as US $279.60 (around P17,000) to as high as $1,747.50 (around P109,000) on a verified resale ticket. “I can’t wait to have her out there late at night and see all the Filipino crowd behind her. It’s going to be really special,” Butorac said. Eala, seeded 17th, is meeting Stoiana for the second time. They first faced each other at an W100 International Tennis Federation (ITF) tournament in Landisville, Pennsylvania where the 21-year-old Filipina won in straight sets. On paper, Eala holds a big advantage against Stoiana. The Filipina enjoys a career-high ranking at No. 18 and is coming off a breakthrough WTA Tour title victory at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington DC a few weeks ago. Eala is also on a mission of eclipsing her previous best Grand Slam finish of a fourth-round appearance at the Wimbledon a few months back. A victory for Eala would arrange her a second-round meeting with the winner between Oleksandra Oliynykova of Ukraine and wildcard Reese Brantmeier of the United States.

Otoc, Sanchez banner field as Digos jrs netfest unwraps. Julius Otoc and Cyrelmae Sanchez headline a strong field seeking top honors and ranking points as the MJFC Araw ng Digos Juniors Age Group Tennis Championships fires off Wednesday, Sept. 2, at the Digos City courts in Davao del Sur. Otoc and Sanchez are seeded No. 1 in the boys’ and girls’ 18-and-under division, respectively, with both also seeing action in the 16-and-U category, albeit with lower seeding. The weeklong Group 2 tournament ushers in the Palawan Pawnshop Mindanao swing, which also features legs in Sultan Kudarat and Cotabato. Seeking to spoil the top seeds’ bids for championship honors and valuable ranking points are Jhazz Fernando, Kurt Alcantara and Shaun Globasa in the boys’ 18-and-U division, and Aika Salahuddin, Marxian Sira and Dyan Placa in the girls’ side. Cristiano Calingasan heads the boys’ 16-and-U cast, with Otoc seeded No. 2, followed by Kresthan Belacas, Kyle Ramos, Rein Hayana, Krisnel Batilo, Carlo Eduarte and Richlord Sira. Multi-titled Francine Wong leads the girls’ 16-and-U field, which also includes Justine Gumbao, Sanchez, Teresinha Calingasan, Kyth Solis, Marxian Sira, Placa and Dominique Calingasan. Belacas, another multi-winner in the nationwide junior circuit, tops the boys’ 14-and-under cast alongside Archie Roceta, Xian Sugsi and Andrei Domasing. Wong is likewise tipped to make a strong run in the girls’ 14-and-U division, which includes Gumbao and sisters Teresinha and Dominique Calingasan. Domasing and Arissa Macapendeg headline the youngest 12-and-U division of the tournament, supported by ICON Golf & Sports and the Palawan Group of Companies. The Mindanao swing is part of the nationwide junior tennis series put up by Palawan Pawnshop president and CEO Bobby Castro, whose program seeks to bring competitive junior tennis closer to the countryside, where a growing number of promising players are emerging but often lack opportunities to test themselves in high-level competition. The tournament is hosted by Mayor Josef Fortich Cagas and sanctioned by Philta and Universal Tennis Rating. Aside from the singles events, titles are also at stake in the boys’ and girls’ 14-and-U and 18-and-U doubles competitions. Meanwhile, Sultan Kudarat will host the next leg on Sept. 10-15 for the Bagong Pilipinas age-group tournament, with the Capital Indoor and Outdoor courts in Isulan serving as venue. The circuit then winds up in Cotabato with the Kidapawan Juniors Championship on Sept. 16-22 at the Kidapawan City courts.

GSIS returns ₱19 billion to 700,000 members through loan relief programs. State-run pension fund Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) has returned ₱19 billion to more than 700,000 members through its Balik Ginhawa loan relief programs as of end-August, freeing up funds that government workers can use for household expenses instead of loan payments. In a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1, GSIS said the refunds covered nearly 1.3 million loan contracts, with ₱8.9 billion credited under the first Balik Ginhawa program and another ₱10.1 billion through the enhanced Balik Ginhawa 2. The programs provide qualified members with refunds corresponding to loan payments covered by a moratorium, allowing them to temporarily redirect money otherwise earmarked for amortizations toward expenses such as tuition, household bills, medical needs, groceries, and home repairs. For instance, GSIS said a government employee paying ₱20,000 in monthly loan amortizations could free up as much as ₱120,000 in spending power over six months. “Balik Ginhawa is about putting money back into the hands of our members and letting them decide where their families need it most. That can make a real difference in a family’s life,” GSIS President and General Manager (PGM) Wick Veloso said. The first Balik Ginhawa program began on March 1, followed by Balik Ginhawa 2 on July 1. Unlike a new loan, the programs provide relief without requiring members to take on additional debt to obtain funds for immediate needs. With two months remaining before the program closes on Oct. 31, GSIS said the total amount returned to members is nearing the ₱20-billion mark. Veloso urged qualified members who have yet to avail themselves of Balik Ginhawa 2 to apply before the deadline. “We want every qualified member to benefit. There is still time to apply for Balik Ginhawa 2, and we encourage our members not to wait until the last minute,” Veloso said. GSIS said Balik Ginhawa forms part of its broader effort to translate the pension fund’s financial strength into benefits for its members. “Our goal is not simply to build a stronger GSIS. Our goal is to make that strength felt by every member and every family we serve. Ang pondo ng GSIS ay para sa ginhawa ng ating mga miyembro,” Veloso said.

UN spotlights nuclear weapon states' refusal to ratify test ban treaty at divisive time. UNITED NATIONS (AP) — With the U.S., Russia, China and other countries that have nuclear weapons refusing to ratify the treaty that bans atomic testing, the United Nations warned on Monday that any new test could trigger another arms race. U.N. disarmament chief Izumi Nakamitsu told the U.N. General Assembly that it was meeting to mark International Day against Nuclear Tests at a time of “deep geopolitical tension, growing division and diminishing trust,” as well as concern about the possible resumption of testing. Late last year, the United States and Russia, which have the world’s largest nuclear arsenals, threatened to resume nuclear testing, setting off global alarm bells. President Donald Trump accused Russia and China of conducting tests, which they deny. “Even contemplating such a course is dangerous,” Nakamitsu warned. “Any resumption would erode decades of restraint, deepen mistrust and risk triggering reciprocal tests and an arms race. This must never become reality.” When the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty was adopted in 1996, it had a very high bar to enter into force. It had to be ratified by 44 specific countries, and nine of them have not yet done so. The United States, China, Iran, Egypt and Israel have signed but not ratified the treaty. India, Pakistan and North Korea have neither signed nor ratified. Russia signed and ratified, but revoked its ratification in 2023. Robert Floyd, head of the organization overseeing the treaty known as the CTBT, told the General Assembly that Tonga’s ratification last month brings the number of parties to the treaty to 179. Since 1945, he said the planet has seen more than 2,000 nuclear test explosions, but in the past three decades fewer than 12. He cautioned, however, that “the international scene is tense, full of mistrust,” including about nuclear testing If nuclear testing resumes, Floyd warned, the result would be new technologically advanced nuclear arsenals, soaring risks of nuclear miscalculation, and “devastation from nuclear `bad luck.’” The International Day Against Nuclear Tests was established to commemorate the Aug. 29, 1991, shutdown of the former Soviet nuclear test site at Semipalatinsk, now in Kazakhstan, which saw 456 nuclear tests, Floyd said. It also puts a spotlight on victims of the atomic era. Tina Cordova described to the U.N. General Assembly how five generations of her family were exposed to radiation that began with the testing of the first atomic bomb on July 16, 1945, in New Mexico — and how every succeeding generation until today has suffered from cancer. “We were never warned before or after of the danger, so we lived our lives off the land as we always did," said Cordova, who co-founded an organization called the Tularosa Basin Downwinders Consortium 21 years ago to spotlight the negative health effects of radiation suffered by the people of New Mexico. She stressed that they were not alone. Nuclear testing took place around the world, she said, and people living in Guam, Tahiti, Kazakhstan and Aboriginal areas of Australia as well as in Idaho, Utah, Arizona, Nevada, Colorado and Montana were also exposed — including uranium workers and their families. “We’re the people that became the collateral damage to the development and testing of nuclear devices and were left to deal with the consequences on our own,” Cordova said. “It is why we fight for acknowledgment and assistance.”

Carney’s Liberals sweep 3 special elections in Canada as voters back his stand against Trump. TORONTO (AP) — Canada's Liberals swept three special elections Monday in a result that showed voters backing Prime Minister Mark Carney for standing up against U.S. President Donald Trump. The Canadian Press, Canada’s national news agency, projected Liberal victories in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord in Quebec, Beaches-East York in Toronto and North Vancouver-Capilano in British Columbia. Carney said the results amounted to an endorsement of his government’s approach. “At this consequential time for Canada, voters have placed their trust in our government’s plan,” he said in a statement. The Quebec result was the most dramatic shift. Liberal Daniel Gobeil was projected to win big in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord, a district held by the opposition Conservatives since 2018. The region is home to aluminum producers, dairy farms and other industries caught in the escalating trade war. “This victory means we can maintain Canadian unity all across the country,” Gobeil said. The other two seats were previously held by Liberals. In British Columbia, Carney’s former deputy chief of staff Braeden Caley won North Vancouver-Capilano. “The United States is getting a message tonight. Our leader has the support of the Canadian people,” Liberal lawmaker Hedy Fry told the Canadian Broadcasting Corp. in an interview. U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed Aug. 21 after the two sides failed to reach a deal, and Trump imposed 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods. Canada responded with plans for tariffs on U.S. products. Trump has escalated his attacks on Canada since the talks failed. He signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America," and U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Monday that Canada had limited leverage in the dispute because the U.S. economy is roughly 13 times larger. Trump has repeatedly talked about making Canada the 51st state. Carney has accelerated efforts to deepen economic ties with Europe and other partners. The Liberal sweep would bring Carney’s party to 173 seats in the 343-seat House of Commons, further strengthening its position in Parliament. The special elections were called after the lawmakers who previously held the three seats resigned from Parliament earlier this year. Daniel Béland, a political-science professor at McGill University, said the Liberal sweep showed Carney retaining strong support across regions, but called the Quebec result the most significant. He said the easy win in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord likely reflected, in part, the popularity in Quebec of Carney’s Aug. 21 decision “to pull the plug on trade negotiations with the White House.” Béland said the Conservative collapse there was also bad news for leader Pierre Poilievre. The party won the riding with 34% of the vote last year but fell to about 13% and third place Monday. “These numbers do look bad,” he said. Carney won Canada’s election last year, fueled by public anger over Trump’s annexation threats, and he has vowed to reduce Canada’s reliance on the U.S.

BIR destroys illicit vapes with over ₱1.5-billion tax liability. The Bureau of Internal Revenue’s (BIR) Manila regional office has destroyed 240,550 illicit vape products seized in the city and Palawan province with tax liability amounting to more than ₱1.5 billion. In a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1, BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza said the destruction last Aug. 24 at DIGAMA Waste Management Facility in Porac town, Pampanga province was part of the agency’s continuing campaign against the illegal manufacture, importation, distribution, and sale of vape products. “Enforcement does not end with seizure. We must permanently remove illicit vape products from the market and hold accountable those behind their illegal manufacture, importation, distribution, and sale,” Mendoza said. Manila Revenue Regional Director Remir Macatangay said his office has expanded its operations from retail stores to warehouses, resulting in a major enforcement action against Tap Fog Philippines, which he described as the BIR’s largest single illicit vape operation. He said the destruction underscores intensified efforts to prevent illicit vape products from returning to the market and to protect government revenues from tax evasion.

PNP beefs up security in pumping stations pver cable theft threat. The Philippine National Police (PNP) tasked policemen in Metro Manila to strengthen security measures around pumping stations and other flood-control facilities following the theft of vital equipment that disrupted flood mitigation operations in Metro Manila. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. also warned that any person who would be caught stealing or buying the stolen items from pumping stations would be dealt with aggressive legal measures. “The Philippine National Police strongly condemns the theft of vital components from government pumping stations. These are not ordinary property crimes because they can compromise flood-control operations and put lives and property at risk,” said Nartatez. The directive follows the reported theft of around eight to 10 meters of grounding cable from the Navotas pumping station, which caused the facility to malfunction amid severe flooding in Metro Manila. Malacañang earlier vowed to run after those involved in the incident, and those who would dare to steal cable and other items from pumping stations, noting the importance of the role of the facilities in addressing floods in Metro Manila. Nartatez said police stations were directed to coordinate with the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), local government units, and facility operators to secure critical infrastructure, particularly in flood-prone areas. “I have directed concerned police units to coordinate with local governments and facility operators, intensify security and conduct immediate investigations to identify and arrest those responsible,” Nartatez said. The theft of pumping station components can disrupt the operation of facilities relied upon to reduce floodwaters, the top cop stressed, and replacing stolen equipment also requires public funds and may delay efforts to address flooding.

United Arab Emirates says it intercepted an Iranian drone over its territorial waters. DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — The United Arab Emirates said that it intercepted an Iranian drone over its waters Monday, an attack that comes after the United States and Iran exchanged fire over the weekend for the first time in a month. Iranian officials said two people were killed and several others wounded in the U.S. attack Sunday night on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded by launching missiles at U.S. sites in Jordan, which were intercepted. During the lull in fighting, the U.S. has been ratcheting up economic pressure on Iran with the hope of forcing concessions out of Tehran, including reopening the Strait of Hormuz to shipping. After the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, Iran established a chokehold on the vital strait, through which a fifth of the world's traded oil passed in peacetime, slowing ship traffic to a trickle. That has roiled the global economy, raising prices worldwide for energy and other goods. As the fighting resumed, the price of Brent crude oil, the international standard, climbed above $90, up about 25% from the start of the war, presenting a growing problem for U.S. President Donald Trump before the midterm elections. A return to open conflict would be dangerous for the region, where Iran has targeted U.S. military bases and infrastructure in Gulf countries since the war began. In the wake of the renewed violence, Anwar Gargash, a diplomatic adviser to the UAE’s president, said on social media that “the state of neither war nor peace cannot be a sustainable solution.” He called for a political solution that would return normal navigation to the Strait of Hormuz, but also a “more realistic approach” than the June memo of understanding between Iran and the U.S., which, he said, “failed to outline a practical and acceptable” road map. UAE says Iranian attack is a ‘dangerous escalation’ In a short statement earlier, the UAE Defense Ministry said it “dealt with” an Iranian drone that was detected over its waters approaching from Iran. There were no reports of damage. “This dangerous escalation constitutes a blatant violation of the UAE’s sovereignty, security, and stability, and a direct threat to the safety of its citizens and residents,” the Foreign Ministry said. The Defense Ministry later issued a second statement denying a claim by the Iranian army that the Al Minhad Air Base in Dubai had been targeted, saying it was false. In the wake of the U.S. attack on Sunday, Iran's military warned that any further U.S. attacks would draw a far heavier response, including strikes on bases or other points from which attacks against Iran are launched, state-run IRNA reported. “The U.S. military has no choice but to leave the region,” the statement from Iran’s Armed Forces General Staff and the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said. Trump on Monday didn’t rule out the possibility of further strikes on Iran. “We’ll see what happens,” he told reporters. Iran says it has right to defend itself and will ‘respond decisively’ Speaking after the first day of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's summit in Kyrgyzstan, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the U.S. must abide by the June memo, state television reported. Araghchi said Iran would continue defending its rights and that the solution to ending the conflict remained “completely clear.” The summit brings together a group billed as a counterweight to U.S. global influence, and includes Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkia was scheduled to meet with Putin on the sidelines Tuesday. US weekend attack comes after weeks of rising economic pressure Meantime, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent opened meetings of the Group of 20 finance ministers in North Carolina on Monday, as Washington pressures other countries to help the U.S. economically isolate Iran. The shifting strategy centers on threats to punish any country or entity that conducts business with Tehran. Two weeks ago, the UAE suspended all trade with Iran after saying it had come under renewed fire from Iran with two missiles splashing down harmlessly in the Persian Gulf. Iran denied the attack. Bessent later suggested it was pressure from Washington that led to the UAE decision. Trump stressed last week that he is “not in a hurry” to get Iran back to the negotiating table, and he continues making the case that the Islamic Republic’s leadership is on the ropes. Appointments to Iran’s senior security leadership in the past month, however, have signaled Tehran’s defiance after weathering decades of sanctions. US military says strike on Iranian rocket launchers 'precise’ On Sunday, U.S. Central Command said it struck Iranian launchers after observing forces with Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military said last week that it had completed clearing sea mines from the waterway’s international shipping routes. U.S. military officials disputed Iran’s claim that the latest American strikes were an act of aggression, calling them a “limited, precise action” against what they said were minelaying forces. Iranian state television later showed what it said were ballistic missiles being fired at American bases in Jordan, and Jordan’s military said it intercepted eight that had entered its airspace. The last time the U.S. military confirmed targeting Iran was July 29, when it announced a “heavy wave of strikes” on dozens of Revolutionary Guard targets.

Wushu Arena PH triumphant in int'l tourney. Wushu Arena Philippines, a traditional martial arts school based at Fisher Mall, Quezon City, concluded its campaign at the 2026 International Traditional Wushu Championship hosted by the International Kung Fu Union Federation, securing 2 gold, 16 silver, and 18 bronze medals across traditional internal and external wushu styles. The 15-athlete delegation — Luyi Corpuz, Anton Sesdoyro, Armando Soriano Jr., Diane Basa, Faith Dapon, Ishy Tantiangco, Jhune Beatriz, John T Duran, Juana Marcelino, Phoebe Ragos-Ty, Reena Cabugao, Sha Liwanag, Sia Villarosa, Sunshine Reyes, and Laurice Ricamara — competed in Children A, Children B, Youth Group, Junior Group A, and Junior Group B divisions in disciplines ranging from Shaolin Barehand and DitangQuan to Emei Sword, Kinarra Staff, and Taichi Duilian. Faith Dapon and Luyi Corpuz brought home the team's two gold medals in Shuang Shanzi and Lian Ren Bu Quan respectively. The team entered the tournament as IKUF's officially designated Kung Fu team for the July–August 2026 championship cycle. Head Coach Arra Jeuneze Corpuz, a certified IKUF international judge for internal arts and Taichi, also served as an External and Internal Kung Fu Judge for western countries during the same competition. The result builds on the school's existing international track record of well over a hundred medals accumulated across the Hong Kong International Wushu Championships and the Emei Cup International Wushu Championships in Chengdu, China. Recognition beyond the mat Alongside the team's competitive results, Arena Fitness Dojo and Wushu Arena Philippines have been named a finalist for the Ten Outstanding UN SDG Awards (TOUSA) People Award and a shortlistee for the Zero Project 2027 Awards under the #ZeroCall27 cycle, run by Austria's Essl Foundation — two international recognitions tied to the program's "Movement Is for Every Body" advocacy rather than to competition results. "This result belongs to every athlete who showed up to train even on the days it was hard," said Corpuz. "We built this program on the idea that traditional wushu, done right, can compete anywhere in the world — and our athletes just proved that." An inclusive model that is getting global attention Unlike many competitive wushu programs, Wushu Arena Philippines operates under an open-door policy — welcoming children, adults, seniors, and students with special needs regardless of prior experience or athletic background. This philosophy previously earned the school recognition as an official member of the Martial Arts Coalition for Sustainable Development (MCS), a UN ECOSOC-linked coalition advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, making it one of the only Philippine organizations on the coalition's international map. About the team Head Coach Arra Jeuneze Corpuz is a 2nd Degree Black Belt (Nidan) in Aikido under Aikido Philippines and Aikikai Hombu Dojo Japan, a two-time Excellent Coach Awardee from the Hong Kong and Chengdu international competitions, and an Overseas Wushu Ambassador Awardee. Supporters can stay updated on the team's ongoing achievements and future endeavors by following their journey on Facebook: fb.com/wushuartsacademy or their website: https://sites.google.com/view/teacherarra/wushu-kung-fu

Why leptospirosis remains a serious threat long after people wade through contaminated water. During the rainy season, especially when there is widespread flooding, doctors brace for the inevitable deluge of leptospirosis cases. Infectious diseases doctors like me, along with kidney doctors (nephrologists) and lung doctors (pulmonologists), are usually called upon to see the sickest patients. While most people infected with leptospirosis only develop mild symptoms, severe leptospirosis can manifest without much warning, progress quickly, and can be fatal. Leptospirosis is caused by a spiral-shaped bacteria that is usually found in rodent urine. Other animals such as dogs and cats can harbor Leptospira species, but it is not as common in these animals. Leptospirosis is usually acquired when wading through flood waters contaminated by rat urine. Other less common ways to get leptospirosis are by ingesting food contaminated with rodent urine and feces, as well as eating poorly cooked meat that is infected with Leptospira. The usual incubation period (time from exposure to symptoms) for leptospirosis is five to 14 days, but in rare cases can be as little as two days or as long as 30 days. Common symptoms of leptospirosis include fever, muscle pain (especially in the calf muscles), fatigue, and headache. Some people develop conjunctival suffusion, which manifests as redness and swelling in the whites of the eyes that can look like sore eyes. Not all these symptoms may be present, and a lot of people only develop milder manifestations, which can get better on their own even without proper treatment. However, a significant number of patients who are not properly treated with antibiotics progress to severe leptospirosis, which is a life-threatening condition. Signs and symptoms of severe leptospirosis include jaundice (yellowing of the skin), decreased urine output, dark color of the urine, abdominal pain, and shortness of breath. This can lead to coughing up blood, bleeding in the mouth, gums, or stool, and low blood pressure. People who have been exposed to flood water, even if they have intact skin with no wounds, should seek medical attention as soon as possible. A doctor or healthcare worker can determine the degree of exposure and prescribe antibiotic prophylaxis with doxycycline or an alternative agent. Prophylaxis works best when given as close to the time of exposure as possible and becomes less effective the longer the delay. When there are large numbers of people exposed, local government units try to make doxycycline available through the barangay health centers following proper medical assessment by barangay healthcare personnel. This medical evaluation is important because the dosing and duration of antibiotics are different for people with intact skin versus those with open wounds or those who inadvertently swallow contaminated water. Continuing exposure to flood water may need periodic administration of prophylaxis. Moreover, antibiotics like doxycycline are prescription-only drugs that can have side effects. Doxycycline can cause heartburn, photosensitivity, rashes, and (in women) vaginal yeast infections. Doxycycline should not be given concurrently with dairy products since milk can inactivate it. Doxycycline should not be given to pregnant women or women who might be pregnant. There are alternatives to doxycycline which a properly qualified obstetrician can prescribe. Children, especially those below 12 years old, should also not be given doxycycline without proper evaluation by a pediatrician. Never take an antibiotic without proper medical evaluation. Aside from potential side effects, unnecessary antibiotic intake can lead to the development of bacterial drug resistance, and the antibiotic may no longer work when we actually need it. If a person develops any of the symptoms of leptospirosis within the two- to 30-day incubation period, they should immediately seek medical care. This should be done even if that person took doxycycline for prophylaxis after exposure. Doxycycline prophylaxis is not a guarantee that one won't get leptospirosis, especially if it is taken more than 72 hours after the exposure. While antibiotic prophylaxis isn't 100 percent effective at preventing infection, it can help decrease the risk of developing severe leptospirosis. Mild to moderate leptospirosis can usually be treated with oral antibiotics and careful monitoring. These patients may not need to be admitted to the hospital if the laboratory results are normal or near normal. Close follow-up is essential since some of these patients can progress to severe leptospirosis even with proper treatment. Patients with severe leptospirosis need to be admitted to the hospital immediately and given intravenous antibiotics such as penicillin or ceftriaxone. Severe leptospirosis can adversely affect the kidneys, the liver, and/or the lungs. Patients with kidney failure from leptospirosis may need urgent dialysis. Early dialysis can help the kidneys recover. If the kidney failure isn't treated promptly, the patient may end up on permanent dialysis, if he or she survives the illness. Patients with liver failure from severe leptospirosis (also known as Weil's disease) have a high chance of dying. They need good supportive care and may need blood products to prevent bleeding since the liver makes the clotting factors for the body. Perhaps the most dreaded complication of leptospirosis is pulmonary hemorrhage. Patients who bleed into their lungs are at a very high risk of dying. They usually need to be hooked up to the ventilator and may need strong medicines like high-dose corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide (an immunosuppressant medication) to modulate the extreme inflammatory response from severe leptospirosis. Even with the best care, we lose a lot of these patients. As I write this, I am the supervising infectious diseases consultant for adult charity patients at the emergency room at our government hospital, and we are seeing a large surge of severe leptospirosis cases. Some patients have already died. These cases were likely infected two weeks prior, and since we’ve had non-stop rains and floods since then, this is just the beginning. Leptospirosis can kill you. Avoid wading in flood waters, use protective gear if you can, and get doxycycline prophylaxis from a healthcare provider or the barangay health center if you are exposed. If you develop symptoms, see your doctor for proper care before it gets worse.

Boransing says Army youth summits predated VP Duterte's DepEd confidential funds use by nearly 20 years. The Philippine Army had been conducting Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) for almost two decades before impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte became Department of Education (DepEd) secretary, Col. Manaros Boransing II testified before senator-judges on Tuesday, Sept. 1. Boransing's revelation belied claims that the 2023 summits were created by DepEd or were dependent on the agency’s confidential funds--the alleged misuse of which was the subject matter of the Senate impeachment court. At any rate, Boransing acknowledged that DepEd joined the interagency planning when schools and students began to be involved. He described the program during direct examination by private prosecutor, layweecReynaldo Robles on day 20 of respondent Duterte’s impeachment trial. “The [YLS] is a long-time Philippine Army program or Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) program,” Boransing said. He described YLS as a response to the recruitment of students and out-of-school youth by violent extremist groups in areas affected by insurgency or terrorism. “The first official, according to the Army’s historical records, the first record was 2002 in Southern Tagalog,” he testified. Boransing recalled that the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division had conducted a summit in Jolo, Sulu as early as 2005. The number of activities varied with the threat level, but the program continued regularly. “It’s definitely annually...It is part of the regular program of the Philippine Army if it is requested by our subordinate unit,” added the military official. Duterte was DepEd secretary from 2022 to 2024. Boransing issued certification on Jan. 1, 2024, covering eight YLS activities with 531 participants and 53 Information Education Campaign (IEC) activities with 9,428 participants in 2023. The Army led the YLS while bringing in local governments, schools, police and other stakeholders. “Well, sir, it’s the Army, and we try to have the local government unit involved as much as possible,” he said. The program’s long history did not mean the Army acted alone; an interagency technical working group selected particular venues after assessing local conditions. “There were some inputs from DepEd, sir, because some of the areas are schools, and many of the participants are students. So definitely, they were involved in the planning and the choosing of the areas,” the witness testified. He described those inputs as school locations, academic schedules and permission to speak with students. He could not say whether they were products of confidential operations. He said the Army budgeted for its own role in YLS, local governments supported youth delegates and participating agencies paid their respective expenses. “It’s part of the regular budget, sir,” Boransing said of the Army’s participation. Boransing's testimony showed that the YLS predated Duterte’s DepEd tenure, operated as a regular Army program and could proceed without receiving confidential funds from DepEd. While the Interagency coordination can explain why DepEd officials or students were present, it cannot be established that confidential informers were paid, that they supplied intelligence or that their information caused the activities certified by Boransing. DepEd later attached Boransing’s certifications to its April 17, 2024 response to COA Audit Observation Memorandum No. 2024-015. The AOM sought proof about the reported rewards totaling ₱15.54 million given to informants for the successful information-gathering or surveillance. Certifications for attendance only Boransing testified that he issued the document as a routine certification of activities and participation—not as his verification of DepEd’s confidential fund transactions. The Jan. 1, 2024 certification recorded eight YLS activities with 531 participants and 53 Information Education Campaign (IEC) activities with 9,428 participants in schools within the 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division’s area of operations. Robles then replayed in court Boransing’s Oct. 17, 2024 testimony at the House of Representatives to establish why the Army issued such documents. The latter affirmed that account under oath before the impeachment court. It did not name a DepEd informer, describe intelligence, record a reward payment or trace the ₱15.54 million later associated with DepEd’s confidential fund response to state auditors. Boransing said Army programs regularly brought together national agencies, local governments, schools and community groups. Participants commonly requested proof of attendance or involvement. “When we participate in activities of one or many agencies, many agencies ask for certifications of attendance,” Boransing said. “We assumed that the certification was also for that purpose...A lot of other national government agencies and local government units ask for certifications in that manner also,” he added. Boransing said then-DepEd Undersecretary Nolasco Mempin sought the document through the Army chain of command. The document’s text remained narrow--it listed activities, participants and locations, but it did not state that DepEd funded the Army programs. It also did not certify that information supplied by a paid informer caused an activity to occur. Likewise, it contained no acknowledgment from a reward recipient and no description of an intelligence product.

Meralco advances nuclear plans with $2.8-million US-backed study. Manuel V. Pangilinan-led Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) and its power generation arm, Meralco PowerGen Corp. (MGEN), have tapped United States (US)-based engineering firm Sargent & Lundy and local partner AMH Philippines Inc. (AMH) to assess the viability of deploying small modular reactors (SMRs) in the country as nuclear energy enters its pre-development phase. In a statement on Tuesday, Sept. 1, MGEN said the partnership is part of the $2.8-million technical assistance (TA) program funded by the US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), which was formally announced in February 2026. The study aims to provide One Meralco with a data-driven basis to determine the feasibility, timing, and integration strategy for incorporating SMRs into the nation’s future energy mix. A dedicated SMR working group has been established within One Meralco to lead the initiative alongside Sargent & Lundy and AMH, with target completion set for the fourth quarter of 2027. Under the engagement, Sargent & Lundy will execute a vendor-neutral assessment aligned with International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) standards and global best practices. The scope covers technology assessment, site selection, grid integration, financial planning, and decision-making frameworks. MGEN President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Emmanuel Rubio said the collaboration would allow the company’s nuclear roadmap to move into a more actionable, data-driven assessment under its nuclear energy strategic transition (NEST) program. “As we advance this USTDA-funded study, MGEN remains committed to exploring safe, reliable, and low-carbon technologies such as SMRs as we work to secure the Philippines’ long-term energy future and support the country’s economic growth,” Rubio added. Beyond technical evaluations, the study features a series of dedicated workshops designed to build technical capacity among key energy stakeholders, including MGEN, the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Philippine Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (PhilATOM). MGEN Head of Strategic Energy Transition Felino M. Bernardo emphasized that the initiative addresses both operational and regulatory realities. “By bringing together a dedicated internal working group, alongside global and local experts, we are undertaking a comprehensive assessment that considers the technical, financial, and regulatory realities of the Philippine setting,” Bernardo said. “The study goes beyond identifying suitable technologies and potential sites. It will also build the technical capacity and decision-making frameworks that can support MGEN and our national stakeholders well beyond the completion of the study,” he added. - Gabriell Christel Galang

P1.9-M smuggled cigarettes from Cebu intercepted in Negros port. BACOLOD CITY - A van loaded with P1.980 million worth of suspected illicit cigarettes from Cebu was intercepted by authorities before midnight in a seaport in Barangay 6, San Carlos City, Negros Occidental on Monday, Aug. 31. Police Lt. Col. Nazer Canja, San Carlos police chief, said they were able to track down the vehicle, following a report on the alleged cigarette smuggling operation. Canja said that a 30-year-old driver and 24-year-old helper from Toledo, Cebu voluntarily surrendered 33 master cases of cigarettes with 60 reams per cases. He said that the vehicle was only rented in Cebu, and the two individuals were only tasked to pick-up the items. Canja said these individuals did not reveal any information regarding the person who ordered the items. This follows the series of seizure of P26.6 million worth of the same contraband in Escalante City, Negros Occidental on Aug. 25, P21 million in a seaborne patrol in Sipalay City, Negros Occidental, and P14.6 million in Bago City, Negros Occidental last month.

Japan’s House Foods weighs sale of Curry House CoCo Ichibanya operator. TOKYO —Japan’s House Foods Group Inc. is considering selling listed subsidiary Ichibanya Co., the operator of the Curry House CoCo Ichibanya, or CoCo Ichi, restaurant chain, it was learned on Monday, Aug. 31. The major food maker is apparently looking to streamline its group business structure, according to sources familiar with the matter. In a statement, House Foods said the company is “considering all available options,” including the delisting of Ichibanya, “with a view to enhancing corporate value and shareholder value.” House Foods acquired Ichibanya in 2015 through a tender offer. Ichibanya has remained a publicly listed company since then. Ichibanya, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s top-tier Prime section, was about 51 percent owned by House Foods as of February this year. For the business year that ended in February 2026, Ichibanya reported consolidated sales of ¥65.5 billion, up 7.4 percent from the previous year, and a net profit of ¥2.5 billion, down 19.2 percent. It runs about 1,200 CoCo Ichi restaurants in Japan and some 200 overseas, including the Philippines.

Cebu stuns Abra; Quezon, Biñan triumphs. The Cebu Greats shook the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) 2026 Season with a 74-70 stunner over the Abra Solid North Weavers on Monday, Aug. 31, at the Ynares Center Montalban in Rizal Province. Kint Akiar delivered in the homestretch to complete what Mark Meneses set up, lifting Cebu to its fourth straight win and a 19-5 record in the round-robin elimination phase of the two-division, 26-team tournament. Ariar, a 6-foot-3 find from the Cebu Institute of Technology University and Letran, drilled in a jumper and two free throws in the last 42 seconds as Cebu snapped Abra's hot run at 19 and pulled the Weavers down to 21-2. Ron Dennison also delivered at clutch time, making two charities with 20.3 seconds left, compensating for the two free throws of Abra's Alfred Ryan Batino, only 12.3 seconds to go. Overall, Meneses carried the Greats past the defending champion Weavers with 26 points, 14 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals and 2 blocks in 35 minutes and 29 seconds of play. Meneses was named the SportsPlus best player over Dhon Reverente, with 16 points, 12 in the third quarter, and 4 rebounds; and Ariar, who notched 8 points and 2 rebounds. Abra drew 20 points, 11 rebounds and 2 assists from Dave Ildefonso; 18 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 steals from DJ Fenner; and 8 points and 9 rebounds from John Uduba. With Ildefonso pouring in 12 points and Uduba adding 6, Abra took the half, 38-34, negating Meneses' 16-point effort for Cebu, which is ranked fourth in the South division behind first game winner Quezon Province (16-3), Biñan (19-4) and Batangas City (16-4). Defending champion Abra still paces the North division, towing San Juan and Caloocan, both 18-3, and Ilagan Isabela (13-9). Quezon trounces Manila The Quezon Huskers battered Manila Batang Quiapo, 107-65, to signify their bid for a third straight South division title. Manila led briefly, 17-16, as Joe Gomez De Liano knocked in his first three triple attempts. Quezon, however, clustered 28 straight points bridging the first and second quarters to regain control, 44-17, and never let go. All 15 Huskers, with Cedric Manzano piling 16 and John Abate adding 14, scored as they led by as far as 107-61 with 50.4 seconds left. Biñan thwarts Rizal Biñan quelled Rizal XentroMall's repeated rallies and prevailed, 65-61, in the nightcap. Nic Cabanero shone again for Biñan with 14 points, 14 rebounds and 2 assists; followed by Kenny Rocacurva, with 12 points, 8 rebounds and 4 steals; Carlo Lastimosa, with 11 points and 2 rebounds; Mochael Mabulac, with 10 points, 9 rebounds and 3 assists; and Pamboy Raymundo, with 10 points and 4 assists. Rizal, which saw its five-win streak broken, drew 10 points and 10 rebounds from veteran Mark Yee. Also-ran Manila fell to a league-worst 1-23 card despite Mark Doligon's 20 points and De Liano's 18. The MPBL returns to the Batangas City Coliseum on Tuesday, featuring games between Marikina and Pasig at 3 p.m., San Juan and Mindoro at 5 p.m., and Bataan and Batangas at 7 p.m.

Tour de France champion Pogacar has collarbone surgery after Vuelta crash. BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogačar underwent successful surgery on his left collarbone on Monday, Aug, 31, following a crash over the weekend, his UAE Team Emirates team said. Pogačar broke two bones on Saturday after losing control when a stone rolled across the road during the eighth stage of the Vuelta a España. He attempted to remount his bike following the crash but was unable to continue and walked to an awaiting ambulance. He withdrew from the race. Dr. Xavier Mir performed the operation at Dexus University Hospital in Barcelona. “The procedure went well, and he will remain in the hospital for post-operative monitoring for a few days,” team doctor Adrian Rotunno said in a statement. Before the crash, Pogačar held a commanding lead in the Vuelta and was heavily favored to become the ninth male rider in history to win all three Grand Tours. The Slovenian's next scheduled event is the world road championships from Sept. 20 in Montreal, where he hopes to compete for a third consecutive title if his recovery allows. Meanwhile, the Vuelta resumes on Tuesday following Monday’s rest day, with a 187-kilometer (116-mile) stage between Alcaraz and Elche de la Sierra. It wraps up in Granada on Sept. 13.

Chad Blames Sudan’s Army for Strikes on Convoy cmoore Fri, 08/28/2026 - 12:46 Latest Updates Africa Asia-Pacific Europe Latin America & Caribbean Middle East & North Africa United States Global Issues & Institutions My Reading List Analyst's Notebook / Africa 28 August 2026 2 minutes Chad Blames Sudan’s Army for Strikes on Convoy Crisis Group expert Fulbert Ngodji sheds light on an air raid in Chad that is believed to have destroyed trucks carrying supplies for one of the main belligerents in the Sudanese civil war. Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Fulbert Ngodji Analyst, Central Africa https://www.linkedin.com/in/fulbert-dg-ngodji-459054147/ Related Tags Chad Sudan On 22 August, the Chadian army accused its Sudanese counterpart of attacking a convoy in eastern Chad. In a televised statement , the army spokesman said Sudanese army aircraft and drones had pursued the trucks over 100km into Chad two days earlier before striking them in Mourdi department, Ennedi-Est province. Pro-Sudanese army online platforms circulated images purporting to show the army disabling several vehicles carrying supplies for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group it has been fighting for control of Sudan since April 2023. The Sudanese army has not directly responded to the allegation, merely affirming its “respect for Chad’s sovereignty” in a 27 August statement . Open-source data and confidential sources have allowed Crisis Group to piece together a plausible account of what happened. A convoy of around 200 military pickup trucks reportedly left Libya and crossed Chad en route to Sudan. The Sudanese army or one of its allies then appears to have attacked the trucks near the Chadian border, as part of a months-long aerial campaign to disrupt RSF supply lines from Libya. About 70 vehicles tried to escape by crossing back into Chad, where they were destroyed. Satellite imagery showing smoke rising from the area seems to corroborate the Chadian army’s charge. It is unclear, however, who was driving the trucks and what they were carrying. The Chadian army did not address these questions. The conflict in Sudan has repeatedly spilled into Chad, primarily through an influx of refugees and, more recently, cross-border violence. Since December 2025, Chad’s eastern border has seen at least eleven incursions and drone strikes, which reportedly have killed about 30 civilians and soldiers. N’Djamena has typically sent military reinforcements or closed the border in response, but to this point it had refrained from blaming either of the main warring parties in Sudan. The 22 August statement is a departure from the previous caution, raising concerns that Chad will be drawn deeper into the civil war next door. Not only could Chad’s allegation sharpen tensions with the army-aligned authorities in Khartoum, but it could also reinforce perceptions that N’djamena has chosen sides in Sudan’s war, indirectly supporting the RSF. These perceptions are based on evidence that the United Arab Emirates has been using Chadian territory to provide the RSF with weapons and equipment. N’Djamena and Abu Dhabi have consistently denied these claims. Even so, escalation is unlikely: a confrontation would be costly for both N’Djamena and the Sudanese army. President Mahamat Déby is struggling to contain anger among his Zaghawa ethnic group, which has dominated Chad’s ruling elite since 1990. Many Zaghawa resent the government’s alleged backing of the RSF. The Sudanese army, meanwhile, controls Khartoum and much of central, northern and eastern Sudan, but remains locked in a war of attrition with no end in sight. Still, if the Sudanese army did in fact conduct the strike, its scale sets a dangerous precedent and could pave the way for more attacks by Sudanese belligerents, fuelling risks of a response by N’Djamena. Syria: First Assad-Era Verdicts a Test for Justice. Click to expand Image Atef Najib during a trial session at the Palace of Justice in Damascus, Syria, April 26, 2026. © 2026 AP Photo/Ghaith Alsayed (Amman) – A Syrian court’s first verdicts for crimes committed during the Assad era raise important legal issues the government should urgently address, Human Rights Watch said today. Human Rights Watch released a question-and-answer document on the trial of Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security Branch in Daraa, who was convicted on August 11, 2026, along with former President Bashar al-Assad and six other defendants tried in absentia. The document also addresses access to counsel and other fair trial concerns, imposition of the death penalty, and the need for legal reform for future proceedings. “Prosecuting Assad-era atrocities is an important opportunity to achieve the justice Syrians have sought for over a decade,” said Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “At the same time, the trials so far highlight an urgent need for reforms to ensure that Syria’s justice system can deliver fair, meaningful, and comprehensive accountability.” The eight defendants in the Najib trial were all sentenced to death. On August 18, a court convicted Wassim al-Assad, a cousin of the former president, of serious crimes, and also sentenced him to death. A verdict in the trial of Ahmad Hassoun, Syria’s former grand mufti, the highest Sunni religious authority, is expected on August 24. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty and irreversibility. Accessible public information about these cases has been limited. Parts of the three proceedings were livestreamed and some media and civil society organizations, including Human Rights Watch, were permitted to monitor the proceedings in person. Syrian authorities have said they will publish the full written verdicts. Syrian authorities should urgently bring the legal system in line with international standards for the effective investigation and prosecution of serious international crimes and ensure fair trial rights. They should make criminal proceedings transparent and accessible. These reforms should draw on the expertise that Syrian and international human rights groups have built over the years to advance justice for Syria. “Advancing justice for the litany of serious crimes committed in Syria requires more than just convictions, but building a system that can deliver competent, impartial, and independent justice,” Jarrah said.

Bangladesh: End Indefinite Pretrial Detention of Political Opponents. Click to expand Image Prison vans transport former ministers and leaders of the Bangladesh Awami League party to jail after their court hearing from the Bangladesh International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on November 18, 2024. © Mamunur Rashid/NurPhoto via AP (London) – Bangladeshi authorities should immediately take steps to end the prolonged pretrial detention of politicians and others linked to the deposed Awami League government, Human Rights Watch said today. Police detained thousands of party officials, activists, and supporters after Sheikh Hasina was forced to step down as prime minister in August 2024 following weeks of protests, and hundreds remain in prison without being charged with any crime. Though some officials may have been complicit in the Hasina government’s serious rights violations, many were arrested without apparent evidence on allegations of murdering protesters. Their family members and lawyers allege that the detainees, many of them older people, some with serious health conditions, have been denied basic rights including bail and medical care. At least 10 Awami League office holders, most of whom were not charged with any crime, have died in prison since Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took office in February 2026. “Under one government after another, hundreds of opposition members have been locked up without evidence or due process,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has pledged reform, and as a first step he should end the prolonged arbitrary detention of political opponents.” Instead of pursuing reforms, the government’s new National Human Rights Commission bill—if adopted in its current form—would prevent the new commission from investigating alleged arbitrary arrests. Those detained without charge include former Awami League members of parliament, other former lawmakers that supported Hasina’s administration, and activists, officials, and journalists who had backed the Awami League government. Others, including members of the security forces, are accused of serious international crimes including extrajudicial killings, torture, and disappearances. Some are also accused of corruption. Prosecutors have repeatedly sought to deny bail in cases in which no evidence has been produced. The lower magistrate and district courts have consistently refused bail, and High Court bail orders have been circumvented as government authorities file fresh cases. In one example, ABM Khairul Haque, 82, a former chief justice, was arrested on July 24, 2025, for allegedly murdering a protester. Over the following three months, he was arrested in four more cases, including for corruption. The lower courts denied bail in each of these, though his family told Human Rights Watch he was in poor health and had a heart attack while in prison. The High Court granted the bail applications, but on March 10, 2026, the day before the court granted bail in the final case, the police applied for him to be arrested in two new cases, preventing his release. The lower courts refused bail in both of these new cases, and the High Court on May 12 granted him bail. But before Haque could be released, police filed another murder charge. They alleged he was at a murder scene at exactly the same time as an earlier murder alleged against him, though the two locations are over 10 kilometers apart. The process was repeated once again, with the High Court granting bail and the police, for the third time, filing a further case, with the authorities this time seeking to evade a new High Court bail ruling requiring the police not to “arrest and harass” Haque “unless there is a specific case against him.” He was finally released on August 19 after intervention by the Appellate Division. Throughout this period, he was not charged with any offense. Lawyers for other detainees told Human Rights Watch that they now advise their clients not to seek bail, as if they succeed the police simply file a new case against them. Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal, a domestic court to prosecute international crimes, allows detention without charge beyond one year only in “exceptional circumstances” that are set out in writing. The tribunal has not released on bail any of the over 160 people it has detained, who have no right to appeal bail rejections. Dr. Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury, 81, a former Hasina advisor, was first detained by the tribunal in October 2024 and has now spent 22 months in custody without charge. When he sought bail in April 2026, the tribunal neither allowed bail nor set out any “exceptional circumstances.” It instead adjourned proceedings twice, most recently until the end of August. A former parliament member, Kamal Ahmed Majumder, 75, has also been detained by the tribunal for 22 months. In jail, his family told Human Rights Watch, he suffered gangrene on his foot requiring amputation of three toes and broke his hip when he fell. The tribunal refused bail in July. Many families say that their detained relatives are not receiving adequate medical care. Activists have called for the release of Shahriar Kabir, 75, who suffers chronic ailments and needs a wheelchair. RAM Obaidul Muktadir Chowdhury, 71, has been in detention for 22 months without charge and has serious heart problems. Ramesh Chandra Sen, 85, a former Awami League lawmaker, who was arrested in August 2024 for three cases of murder and an explosives case, remained in detention until his death on February 7, 2026. His family said he was denied proper medication and refused bail. Similar concerns relate to the death of SM Ziaul Haque Zia, 65, a Jamalpur district Awami League member who was already in poor health when he was detained on January 6. He died on April 14, after he was denied bail. International human rights law permits some use of pretrial incarceration or release with conditions. However, such detention should be the exception, not the rule, and should be determined on an individual basis. A judge or equivalent should review the detention of every detained person to consider the legality and necessity of their detention, and anyone so detained is entitled to a speedy trial or release. Any pretrial restrictions must be consistent with the right to liberty, the presumption of innocence, and the right to equality. “A justice system that lets older people die in custody before they are ever charged is not treating pretrial detention as the exceptional measure it always should be,” Pearson said. “The Bangladeshi government should order independent inquiries into all prison deaths under its watch and stop arbitrarily detaining people for prolonged periods without charge.”

Colombia: Armed Groups Expand Child Recruitment.
